bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【晉紀十五】 起閼逢涒 □灘，盡強圉大淵獻，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 15] From Emao Zui□tan through Qiangyu Dayuanxian; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 15] From the cyclical year Emao Zui□tan through Qiangyu Dayuanxian—a span of four years.

sentences.zh: 肅宗明皇帝下太寧二年（

translations.literal: Under the chronicle of the Illustrious Ancestor, Emperor Ming—the second year of Taining (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, second year of Taining (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元三二四年）

translations.literal: Jiashen, corresponding to the year 324 CE)
translations.idiomatic: year Jiashen, AD 324)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，王敦誣周嵩、周莛與李脫謀為不軌，收嵩、莛於軍中，殺之；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wang Dun accused Zhou Song and Zhou Ting of plotting sedition with Li Tuo; he seized Song and Ting in the army camp and killed them;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wang Dun charged Zhou Song and Zhou Ting with plotting treason alongside Li Tuo, seized them in camp, and put them to death;

sentences.zh: 遣參軍賀鸞就沈充於吳，盡殺周札諸兄子；

translations.literal: he sent adjutant He Luan to join Shen Chong in Wu and put to death all the sons of Zhou Zha's elder brothers;
translations.idiomatic: he dispatched his adjutant He Luan to Shen Chong in Wu, who slaughtered every nephew of Zhou Zha's brothers;

sentences.zh: 進兵襲會稽，札拒戰而死。

translations.literal: he advanced to attack Kuaiji; Zha resisted in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: then marched on Kuaiji, where Zha fought to the death in defense.

sentences.zh: 後趙將兵都尉石瞻寇下邳、彭城，取東莞、東海，劉遐退保泗口。

translations.literal: Shi Zhan, commander of troops for Later Zhao, raided Xiapi and Pengcheng, seized Dongguan and Donghai, and Liu Xia withdrew to defend Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhan, Later Zhao's commander of troops, attacked Xiapi and Pengcheng, took Dongguan and Donghai, and Liu Xia fell back to hold Sikou.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史石生擊趙河南太守尹平於新安，斬之，掠五千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng, Inspector of Sizhou, attacked Zhao's Administrator of Henan, Yin Ping, at Xin'an, beheaded him, and returned after plundering more than five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng, inspector of Sizhou, struck Zhao's Henan administrator Yin Ping at Xin'an, killed him, and withdrew after carrying off more than five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 自是二趙構隙，日相攻掠，河東、弘農之間，民不聊生矣。

translations.literal: From this the two Zhao states developed a rift and raided each other daily; between Hedong and Hongnong the people could no longer make a living.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two Zhao regimes were at odds and attacked each other day after day, until the people between Hedong and Hongnong could scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 石生寇許、穎，俘獲萬計；

translations.literal: Shi Sheng raided Xu and Ying and took captives numbering in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng raided Xu and Ying and took tens of thousands captive;

sentences.zh: 攻郭誦於陽翟，誦與戰，大破之，生退守康城。

translations.literal: he attacked Guo Song at Yangdi; Song engaged him in battle and inflicted a great defeat; Sheng withdrew to defend Kangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: he besieged Guo Song at Yangdi, but Song met him in battle and routed his forces, forcing Sheng to fall back and hold Kangcheng.

sentences.zh: 後趙汲郡內史石聰聞生敗，馳救之，進攻司州刺史李矩、穎川太守郭默，皆破之。

translations.literal: Shi Cong, Interior Minister of Jijun in Later Zhao, heard of Sheng's defeat and rushed to rescue him; he advanced to attack Li Ju, Inspector of Sizhou, and Guo Mo, Administrator of Yingchuan, and defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Cong, interior minister of Jijun under Later Zhao, learned of Sheng's defeat, he hurried to his aid and marched against Inspector Li Ju of Sizhou and Administrator Guo Mo of Yingchuan, defeating both.

sentences.zh: 成主雄，後任氏無子，有妾子十餘人，雄立其兄蕩之子班為太子，使任後母之。

translations.literal: Lord Xiong of Cheng, Empress Ren had no sons, and he had more than ten sons by concubines; Xiong established Ban, son of his elder brother Dang, as heir apparent and had Empress Ren act as his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xiong of Cheng had no son by Empress Ren, though more than a dozen sons by his concubines; Xiong named Ban, son of his late brother Dang, crown prince and had Empress Ren rear him as her own.

sentences.zh: 群臣請立諸子，雄曰：「吾兄，先帝之嫡統，有奇材大功，事垂克而早世，朕常悼之。

translations.literal: The ministers asked that one of his own sons be made heir; Xiong said, "My elder brother was the legitimate line of the former emperor, possessed extraordinary talent and great merit, and died young when success was near at hand—I have long grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his ministers urged him to name one of his own sons, Xiong said, "My elder brother was the former emperor's legitimate heir, a man of rare ability who won great victories, yet he died young just as triumph was within reach—I have mourned him ever since.

sentences.zh: 且班仁孝好學，必能負荷先烈。」

translations.literal: Moreover Ban is benevolent, filial, and fond of learning—he will surely be able to bear up the achievements of our forebears."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Ban is dutiful, filial, and devoted to learning; he will surely be able to uphold our ancestors' legacy."

sentences.zh: 太傅驤、司徒王達諫曰：「先王立嗣必子者，所以明定分而防篡奪也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xiang and Minister over the Masses Wang Da remonstrated, saying, "Former kings always established heirs from among their own sons in order to clarify the succession and guard against usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xiang and Minister over the Masses Wang Da objected: "Former kings always named their own sons as heirs so that the succession would be clear and usurpation forestalled.

sentences.zh: 宋宣公、吳餘祭，足以觀矣。」

translations.literal: Duke Xuan of Song and Yuji of Wu are sufficient examples to observe."
translations.idiomatic: The cases of Duke Xuan of Song and Yuji of Wu are warning enough."

sentences.zh: 雄不聽。

translations.literal: Xiong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 驤退而流涕曰：「亂自此始矣！」

translations.literal: Xiang withdrew, weeping, and said, "Disorder will begin from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang withdrew in tears and said, "From this moment disorder will begin!"

sentences.zh: 班為人謙恭下士，動遵禮法，雄每有大議，輒令豫之。

translations.literal: Ban was humble toward scholars and in conduct observed ritual propriety; whenever Xiong had a major deliberation, he would have Ban take part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Ban was modest toward men of talent and scrupulous in ritual; whenever Xiong faced a weighty decision, he had Ban take part.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲申，張茂疾病，執世子駿手泣曰：「吾家世以孝友忠順著稱，今雖天下大亂，汝奉承之，不可失也。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day Jiashen, Zhang Mao fell gravely ill; grasping the hand of his heir Jun, he wept and said, "Our family has been renowned for generations for filial piety, friendship, loyalty, and obedience; though the realm is now in great disorder, you must uphold this and must not let it slip."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day Jiashen, Zhang Mao lay gravely ill; taking his heir Jun by the hand, he wept and said, "Our house has been known for generations for filial devotion, brotherly harmony, loyalty, and obedience; though the empire is torn by chaos, you must uphold these virtues and never abandon them."

sentences.zh: 且下令曰：「吾官非王命，苟以集事，豈敢榮之！

translations.literal: He also issued an order, saying, "My offices were not conferred by royal mandate but were taken up merely to accomplish the task—how dare I treat them as honors!
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded: "My titles were never granted by the throne; I accepted them only to get the work done—how could I treat them as glory!

sentences.zh: 死之日，當以白帢入棺，勿以朝服斂。」

translations.literal: On the day of my death, I am to be placed in the coffin wearing a white headcloth—do not bury me in court robes."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, lay me in my coffin wearing only a white headcloth; do not dress me in court regalia for burial."

sentences.zh: 是日，薨。

translations.literal: That same day he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he passed away.

sentences.zh: 愍帝使者史淑在姑臧，左長史汜禕、右長史馬謨等使淑拜駿大將軍、涼州牧、西平公，赦其境內。

translations.literal: The envoy of Emperor Min, Shi Shu, was at Guzang; the Left Chief Clerk Si Yi, the Right Chief Clerk Ma Mo, and others had Shu invest Jun as Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping, and proclaimed an amnesty within their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min's envoy Shi Shu was at Guzang; the left chief clerk Si Yi, the right chief clerk Ma Mo, and others had Shu invest Jun as grand general, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping, and proclaimed an amnesty throughout the domain.

sentences.zh: 前趙主曜遣使贈茂太宰，謚曰成烈王。

translations.literal: Liu Yao, lord of Former Zhao, sent envoys to posthumously confer on Mao the title of Grand Preceptor and give him the posthumous name King Cheng-lie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao of Former Zhao sent envoys to posthumously honor Mao as grand preceptor with the temple name King Cheng-lie.

sentences.zh: 拜駿上大將軍、涼州牧、涼王。

translations.literal: Jun was appointed Grand General Supreme, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was invested as grand general supreme, governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 王敦疾甚，矯詔拜王應為武衛將軍以自副，以王含為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's illness grew severe; he forged an edict appointing Wang Ying as Defender-General of the Martial Guards as his deputy, and Wang Han as Cavalry General-in-Chief with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun grew gravely ill; he forged an edict naming Wang Ying defender-general of the martial guards as his deputy and Wang Han cavalry general-in-chief with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 錢鳳謂敦曰：「脫有不諱，便當以後事付應邪？」

translations.literal: Qian Feng said to Dun, "If the unforeseen should occur, ought the aftermath be entrusted to Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng asked Dun, "If the worst should happen, would you really leave everything to Ying?"

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「非常之事，非常人所能為。

translations.literal: Dun said, "Extraordinary affairs are not what ordinary men can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Dun replied, "Extraordinary undertakings are not for ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 且應年少，豈堪大事！

translations.literal: Moreover Ying is young—how could he bear great affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Ying is still young—how could he shoulder such a burden!

sentences.zh: 我死之後，莫若釋兵散眾，歸身朝廷，保全門戶，上計也；

translations.literal: After my death, it would be best to disband the army and scatter the troops, return to the court's allegiance, and preserve the clan—this is the superior plan;
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, your best course is to disband the army, submit to the court, and preserve our house—that is the high plan;

sentences.zh: 退還武昌，收兵自守，貢獻不廢，中計也；

translations.literal: withdraw to Wuchang, gather troops for self-defense, and not cease tribute—this is the middle plan;
translations.idiomatic: withdraw to Wuchang, hold your forces in defense, and keep sending tribute—that is the middle plan;

sentences.zh: 及吾尚存，悉眾而下，萬一僥倖，下計也。」

translations.literal: while I still live, lead all forces southward and hope for a stroke of luck—this is the inferior plan."
translations.idiomatic: or, while I still breathe, march every man south and gamble on a lucky stroke—that is the low plan."

sentences.zh: 鳳謂其黨曰：「公之下計，乃上策也。」

translations.literal: Feng told his partisans, "The master's inferior plan is in fact the superior strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Feng told his followers, "His 'low plan' is really the best strategy of all."

sentences.zh: 遂與沈充定謀，俟敦死即作亂。

translations.literal: He then joined Shen Chong in a plot to rebel as soon as Dun died.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Chong then agreed to rise in rebellion the moment Dun died.

sentences.zh: 又以宿衛尚多，奏令三番休二。

translations.literal: Because the palace guards were still numerous, he memorialized that they should rest two days out of every three rotations.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the palace guard still too large, he petitioned that each unit serve only one rotation in three.

sentences.zh: 初，帝親任中書令溫嶠，敦惡之，請嶠為左司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had personally entrusted Zhongshu Ling Wen Jiao; Dun hated him and requested that Jiao be made Left Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had placed great trust in Palace Secretary Wen Jiao; Dun resented him and had Jiao transferred to serve as his left chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 嶠乃繆為勤敬，綜其府事，時進密謀以附其欲。

translations.literal: Jiao then feigned diligence and respect, managed all affairs of Dun's headquarters, and from time to time offered secret counsel to suit Dun's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao feigned diligence and deference, took charge of headquarters business, and now and then offered secret advice tailored to Dun's desires.

sentences.zh: 深結錢鳳，為之聲譽，每曰：「錢世儀精神滿腹。」

translations.literal: He formed a deep bond with Qian Feng, built up Feng's reputation, and would say, "Qian Shiyi is brimming with intelligence."
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated a close tie with Qian Feng, burnished Feng's reputation, and would say, "Qian Shiyi is a man whose mind is brimming with talent."

sentences.zh: 嶠素有藻鑒之名，鳳甚悅，深與嶠結好。

translations.literal: Jiao had long borne a name for discerning judgment; Feng was greatly pleased and became deeply friendly with Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was already famed for his discernment; Feng was delighted and grew intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 會丹楊尹缺，嶠言於敦曰：「京尹咽喉之地，公宜自選其才，恐朝廷用人，或不盡理。」

translations.literal: When the post of Governor of Danyang fell vacant, Jiao said to Dun, "The capital governor's post is the throat of the realm; you ought to choose the talent yourself, lest the court's appointment not be fully appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: When the governorship of Danyang fell vacant, Jiao told Dun, "The capital governorship is the empire's throat; you ought to choose the man yourself, lest the court appoint someone unsuitable."

sentences.zh: 敦然之，問嶠：「誰可者？」

translations.literal: Dun agreed and asked Jiao, "Who would do?"
translations.idiomatic: Dun agreed and asked, "Whom do you recommend?"

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「愚謂無如錢鳳。」

translations.literal: Jiao said, "In my humble view no one compares with Qian Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao replied, "In my view no one is better than Qian Feng."

sentences.zh: 鳳亦推嶠，嶠偽辭之，敦不聽，六月，表嶠為丹楊尹，且使覘伺朝廷。

translations.literal: Feng in turn recommended Jiao; Jiao falsely declined, but Dun would not listen. In the sixth month he memorialized to appoint Jiao Governor of Danyang and also had him spy on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Feng reciprocated by recommending Jiao; Jiao pretended to decline, but Dun insisted. In the sixth month he had Jiao appointed governor of Danyang and sent him to watch the court.

sentences.zh: 嶠恐既去而錢鳳於後間止之，因敦餞別，嶠起行酒，至鳳，鳳未及飲，嶠偽醉，以手版擊鳳幘墜，作色曰：「錢鳳何人，溫太真行酒而敢不飲！」

translations.literal: Jiao feared that once he left, Qian Feng would afterward dissuade Dun; at Dun's farewell banquet Jiao rose to offer wine, and when he came to Feng, before Feng could drink Jiao pretended drunkenness, struck Feng's headcloth off with his writing tablet, and said angrily, "Who is Qian Feng, that he dares not drink when Wen Taizhen offers the cup!"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that once he departed Qian Feng would talk Dun out of letting him go, Jiao at the farewell feast rose to pour wine; reaching Feng before he could drink, Jiao feigned drunkenness, knocked Feng's cap off with his writing tablet, and cried, "Who is Qian Feng to refuse a cup from Wen Taizhen!"

sentences.zh: 敦以為醉，兩釋之。

translations.literal: Dun took it as drunkenness and reconciled them both.
translations.idiomatic: Dun dismissed it as drunkenness and smoothed matters over between them.

sentences.zh: 嶠臨去，與敦別，涕泗橫流，出閣復入者再三。

translations.literal: As Jiao was about to depart, he took leave of Dun with tears streaming down his face, leaving the gate and re-entering again and again.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure Jiao bade Dun farewell in floods of tears, leaving the gate only to return again and again.

sentences.zh: 行後，鳳謂敦曰：「嶠於朝廷甚密，而與庾亮深交，未可信也。」

translations.literal: After he had gone, Feng said to Dun, "Jiao is very close to the court and is deeply intimate with Yu Liang—he cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao had left, Feng told Dun, "Jiao is on intimate terms with the court and is close to Yu Liang—he is not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「太真昨醉，小加聲色，何得便爾相讒！」

translations.literal: Dun said, "Taizhen was drunk yesterday and raised his voice a little—how can you slander him so readily!"
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "Taizhen was drunk last night and spoke sharply—that hardly proves he is plotting against us!"

sentences.zh: 嶠至建康，盡以敦逆謀告帝，請先為之備，又與庾亮共畫討敦之謀。

translations.literal: When Jiao reached Jiankang he fully disclosed Dun's rebellious designs to the emperor, asked that preparations be made in advance, and together with Yu Liang plotted the campaign to punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao reached Jiankang he told the emperor everything about Dun's conspiracy, urged immediate preparations, and with Yu Liang drew up plans to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 敦聞之，大怒曰：「吾乃為小物所欺！」

translations.literal: When Dun heard of it he flew into a rage and said, "I have been deceived by a petty fellow!"
translations.idiomatic: When Dun learned of this he raged, "I have been duped by a nobody!"

sentences.zh: 與司徒導書曰：「太真別來幾日，作如此事！

translations.literal: He wrote to Minister over the Masses Dao, "It has been only a few days since Taizhen parted from me, and already he has done this!
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Minister Dao, "Taizhen has been gone only a few days and already he has done this!

sentences.zh: 當募人生致之，自拔其舌。」

translations.literal: I shall raise men to capture him alive and tear out his tongue myself."
translations.idiomatic: I shall hire men to take him alive so I can tear out his tongue with my own hands."

sentences.zh: 帝將討敦，以問光祿勳應詹，詹勸成之，帝意遂決。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign against Dun and consulted Household Counsellor Ying Zhan; Zhan urged that it be carried through, and the emperor's mind was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor resolved to move against Dun, he asked Household Counsellor Ying Zhan, who urged him to go through with it, and his decision was made.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，加司徒導大都督、領揚州刺史，以溫嶠都督東安北部諸軍事，與右將軍卞敦守石頭，應詹為護軍將軍、都督前鋒及朱雀橋南諸軍事，郗鑒行衛將軍、都督從駕諸軍事，庾亮領左衛將軍，以吏部尚書卞壺行中軍將軍。

translations.literal: On the day Dingmao, Minister Dao was made Chief Commander-in-Chief and given charge of Yangzhou; Wen Jiao was made commander of all military affairs in the northern part of Dong'an, and together with General of the Right Bian Dun defended Stone City; Ying Zhan was made Protector-General and commander of the vanguard and all forces south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge; Xi Jian acted as Defender-General and commander of all forces accompanying the emperor; Yu Liang held the post of General of the Left Guard; and Minister of Personnel Bian Hu acted as General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingmao, Minister Dao was named supreme commander and given Yangzhou; Wen Jiao was placed in command of northern Dong'an and, with General Bian Dun of the Right, held Stone City; Ying Zhan became protector-general, commanding the vanguard and all troops south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge; Xi Jian served as defender-general in command of the emperor's escort; Yu Liang held the left guard; and Minister of Personnel Bian Hu acted as central-army general.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒以為軍號無益事實，固辭不受，請召臨淮太守蘇峻、兗州刺史劉遐同討敦。

translations.literal: Xi Jian held that military titles were of no practical benefit and firmly declined to accept them; he asked that Su Jun, Administrator of Linhuai, and Liu Xia, Inspector of Yanzhou, be summoned to join in punishing Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian argued that titles alone would not win the war and firmly declined them, asking that Su Jun, administrator of Linhuai, and Liu Xia, inspector of Yanzhou, be called in to help crush Dun.

sentences.zh: 詔征峻、遐及徐州刺史王邃、豫州刺史祖約、廣陵太守陶瞻等入衛京師。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Jun, Xia, Wang Sui, Inspector of Xuzhou, Zu Yue, Inspector of Yuzhou, Tao Zhan, Administrator of Guangling, and others to enter the capital in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called Jun, Xia, Wang Sui of Xuzhou, Zu Yue of Yuzhou, Tao Zhan of Guangling, and others to march to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 帝屯於中堂。

translations.literal: The emperor encamped in the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took up position in the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 司徒導聞敦疾篤，帥子弟為敦發哀，眾以為敦信死，鹹有奮志。

translations.literal: Minister Dao, hearing that Dun's illness was grave, led his sons and nephews in mourning for Dun; the multitude believed Dun was truly dead, and all were stirred to zeal.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Dao heard that Dun was gravely ill, he led his kinsmen in mourning for him; everyone assumed Dun had died, and spirits rose throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書騰詔下敦府，列敦罪惡曰：「敦輒立兄息以自承代，未有宰相繼體而不由王命者也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Masters of Writing promulgated an edict to Dun's headquarters listing his crimes, saying, "Dun has presumptuously established his elder brother's son to succeed him in his own place—never has a chief minister passed on his position without a royal mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then issued an edict to Dun's headquarters listing his crimes: "Dun has presumptuously named his elder brother's son as his heir—never before has a chief minister transmitted power without the throne's command.

sentences.zh: 頑凶相獎，無所顧忌；

translations.literal: The stubborn and vicious encourage one another and heed nothing;
translations.idiomatic: The wicked egg one another on without restraint;

sentences.zh: 志騁兇丑，以窺神器。

translations.literal: their hearts race with villainy to spy upon the imperial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: their hearts bent on evil, they covet the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 天不長奸，敦以隕斃；

translations.literal: Heaven does not long sustain the wicked—Dun has perished and fallen;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven does not long favor traitors—Dun has already fallen;

sentences.zh: 鳳承凶宄，彌復煽逆。

translations.literal: Feng inherits his villainy and fans rebellion all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Feng carries on his evil and fans the rebellion ever higher.

sentences.zh: 今遣司徒導等虎旅三萬，十道並進；

translations.literal: We now dispatch Minister Dao and others with thirty thousand tiger troops advancing on ten routes at once;
translations.idiomatic: We now send Minister Dao and thirty thousand seasoned troops along ten routes at once;

sentences.zh: 平西將軍邃等精銳三萬，水陸齊勢；

translations.literal: Pacifier of the West Sui and others with thirty thousand elite troops, their land and water forces joining in momentum;
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier of the West Wang Sui and thirty thousand picked troops, advancing by land and water together;

sentences.zh: 朕親統諸軍，討鳳之罪。

translations.literal: We shall personally command the armies to punish Feng's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: We shall personally lead the armies to punish Feng.

sentences.zh: 有能殺鳳送首，封五千戶侯。

translations.literal: Whoever can kill Feng and deliver his head shall be enfeoffed as marquis of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever kills Feng and brings in his head shall receive a marquisate of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諸文武為敦所授用者，一無所問，無或猜嫌，以取誅滅。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials whom Dun appointed shall not be questioned at all—let none harbor suspicion and bring destruction upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials whom Dun appointed shall go unpunished; let none invite destruction through needless suspicion.

sentences.zh: 敦之將士，從敦彌年，違離家室，朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: Dun's officers and soldiers have followed Dun for many years, estranged from their families—We deeply pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's soldiers have followed him for years, far from their homes, and We pity them deeply.

sentences.zh: 其單丁在軍，皆遣歸家，終身不調；

translations.literal: Those who are sole sons in the army shall all be sent home and never again levied for service;
translations.idiomatic: Sole sons in the ranks shall all be sent home and never again conscripted;

sentences.zh: 其餘皆與假三年，休訖還台，當與宿衛同例三番。」

translations.literal: the rest shall all be granted three years' leave; when their rest is finished they shall return to the capital and serve in the palace guard on the same three-rotation schedule."
translations.idiomatic: the rest shall receive three years' leave and, when it ends, return to serve in the palace guard on the usual three-rotation schedule."

sentences.zh: 敦見詔，甚怒，而病轉篤，不能自將；

translations.literal: When Dun saw the edict he was greatly enraged, but his illness grew worse and he could not command the army himself;
translations.idiomatic: Dun was furious when he read the edict, but his illness worsened and he could no longer take the field himself;

sentences.zh: 將舉兵伐京師，使記室郭璞筮之，璞曰：「無成。」

translations.literal: he was about to raise troops to attack the capital and had his secretary Guo Pu divine by hexagram; Pu said, "It will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: as he prepared to march on the capital he had his secretary Guo Pu cast the oracle; Pu said, "You will not succeed."

sentences.zh: 敦素疑璞助溫嶠、庾亮，及聞卦凶，乃問璞曰：「卿更筮吾壽幾何？」

translations.literal: Dun had long suspected that Pu aided Wen Jiao and Yu Liang; when he heard the hexagram was inauspicious he then asked Pu, "Divine again—how long is my lifespan?"
translations.idiomatic: Dun had long suspected Pu of siding with Wen Jiao and Yu Liang; when he heard the ill omen he demanded, "Cast again—how long do I have to live?"

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「思向卦，明公起事，必禍不久。

translations.literal: Pu said, "Reflecting on the previous hexagram—if my lord launches this campaign, disaster will come before long.
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "Judging from the last reading, if you launch this campaign, disaster will follow swiftly.

sentences.zh: 若住武昌，壽不可測。」

translations.literal: If you remain at Wuchang, your lifespan cannot be reckoned."
translations.idiomatic: If you stay at Wuchang, your span of years cannot be foretold."

sentences.zh: 敦大怒曰：「卿壽幾何？」

translations.literal: Dun flew into a rage and said, "How long is your lifespan?"
translations.idiomatic: Dun raged, "And how long is yours?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「命盡今日日中。」

translations.literal: He said, "My fate ends at noon today."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Mine ends at noon today."

sentences.zh: 敦乃收璞，斬之。

translations.literal: Dun then seized Pu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had Pu seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 敦使錢鳳及冠軍將軍鄧岳、前將軍周撫等帥眾向京師。

translations.literal: Dun sent Qian Feng and Champion General Deng Yue, Forward General Zhou Fu, and others to lead the host toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent Qian Feng, Champion General Deng Yue, Forward General Zhou Fu, and others to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 王含謂敦曰：「此乃家事，吾當自行。」

translations.literal: Wang Han said to Dun, "This is a family affair—I ought to go myself."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han told Dun, "This is our family's business; I should go in person."

sentences.zh: 於是以含為元帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han was made commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Han was accordingly made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 鳳等問曰：「事克之日，天子雲何？」

translations.literal: Feng and the others asked, "On the day the affair succeeds, what of the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng and the others asked, "If we prevail, what becomes of the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「尚未南郊，何得稱天子！

translations.literal: Dun said, "He has not yet performed the southern suburb sacrifice—how can he be called Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "He has not yet sacrificed at the southern suburb—how can he be called emperor!

sentences.zh: 便盡卿兵勢，保護東海王及裴妃而已。」

translations.literal: Simply deploy all your military strength to protect the Prince of Donghai and Consort Pei, and no more."
translations.idiomatic: Simply use all your force to protect the Prince of Donghai and Lady Pei, and nothing more."

sentences.zh: 乃上疏，以誅奸臣溫嶠等為名。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial in the name of punishing the treacherous ministers Wen Jiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne under the pretext of punishing the traitors Wen Jiao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬申朔，王含等水陸五萬奄至江寧南岸，人情恟懼。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Renshen, Wang Han and others with fifty thousand troops by land and water suddenly arrived on the south bank of Jiangning; the people's hearts were panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Renshen, Wang Han and fifty thousand men by land and sea suddenly appeared on the south bank of Jiangning, throwing the populace into terror.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠移屯水北，燒朱雀桁以挫其鋒，含等不得渡。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao shifted camp to the north of the river and burned the Vermilion Bird Bridge to blunt their momentum; Han and the others could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao moved his camp north of the river and burned the Vermilion Bird Bridge to blunt their advance, so Han's forces could not cross.

sentences.zh: 帝欲新將兵擊之，聞橋已絕，大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lead troops personally to attack them; when he heard the bridge was destroyed he was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to lead troops against them in person; when he learned the bridge had been burned he was furious.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「今宿衛寡弱，徵兵未至，若賊豕突，危及社稷，宗廟且恐不保，何愛一橋乎！」

translations.literal: Jiao said, "At present the palace guard is few and weak and the summoned troops have not yet arrived; if the rebels burst in like swine, the altars of state will be endangered and even the ancestral temples may not be preserved—what is one bridge to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "Our palace guard is thin and reinforcements have not arrived; if the rebels break through like a herd of boars, the altars of state and even the ancestral temples may fall—what is one bridge beside that!"

sentences.zh: 司徒導遺含書曰：「近承大將軍困篤，或雲已有不諱。

translations.literal: Minister Dao sent Han a letter saying, "We have lately learned that the Grand General's illness is grave and some say the unforeseen has already occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dao wrote to Han: "We have lately heard that the Grand General is gravely ill and that the worst may already have befallen him.

sentences.zh: 尋知錢鳳大嚴，欲肆奸逆；

translations.literal: We soon learned that Qian Feng was making great military preparations and intended to unleash treachery and rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: We soon learned that Qian Feng was mobilizing in force and plotting treason;

sentences.zh: 謂兄當抑制不逞，還蕃武昌，今乃與犬羊俱下。

translations.literal: we thought you, elder brother, would restrain the unruly and return to your fief at Wuchang—yet now you have come down together with dogs and goats.
translations.idiomatic: we thought you would restrain the hotheads and withdraw to Wuchang—yet now you march south alongside dogs and goats.

sentences.zh: 兄之此舉，謂可得如大將軍昔年之事乎？

translations.literal: This action of yours—do you think it can achieve what the Grand General accomplished in years past?
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine this venture can repeat the Grand General's success of years ago?

sentences.zh: 昔年佞臣亂朝，人懷不寧，如導之徒，心思外濟。

translations.literal: In those years wicked ministers threw the court into disorder and men's hearts were unsettled; men such as myself thought only of aiding from without.
translations.idiomatic: In those days wicked ministers threw the court into chaos and honest men looked for help from outside—men like me thought only of lending aid from afar.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise.

sentences.zh: 大將軍來屯於湖，漸失人心，君子危怖，百姓勞弊。

translations.literal: The Grand General came to encamp at Yu and gradually lost men's hearts; gentlemen were in dread and terror, and the common people were worn and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General encamped at Yu and steadily lost the people's hearts; men of honor lived in fear, and the common folk were worn to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 臨終之日，委重安期；

translations.literal: on his deathbed he entrusted weighty affairs to Anqi;
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he entrusted everything to Anqi;

sentences.zh: 安期斷乳幾日？

translations.literal: how many days has Anqi been weaned?
translations.idiomatic: how long has Anqi been off the breast?

sentences.zh: 又於時望，便可襲宰相之跡邪？

translations.literal: and by present reputation can he simply step into the chancellor's footsteps?
translations.idiomatic: And by what standing can he simply step into the chancellor's place?

sentences.zh: 自開闢以來，頗有宰相以孺子為之者乎？

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, has there ever been a chancellor made of a mere child?
translations.idiomatic: Since the world began, has any realm ever made a mere child its chancellor?

sentences.zh: 諸有耳者，皆知將為禪代，非人臣之事也。

translations.literal: all who have ears know that a transfer of the mandate is intended—this is no affair for a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone with ears knows you mean to seize the throne—this is no business for loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 先帝中興，遺愛在民；

translations.literal: the former emperor restored the dynasty and left his loving kindness with the people;
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor restored the dynasty, and his kindness still lives in the people's hearts;

sentences.zh: 聖主聰明，德洽朝野。

translations.literal: the sage ruler is intelligent and his virtue pervades court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: the sage emperor is wise, and his virtue fills court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 兄乃欲妄萌逆節，凡在人臣，誰不憤歎！

translations.literal: Yet you, elder brother, would rashly nurture treason—among all who serve as subjects, who does not burn with anger and sigh!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would rashly hatch treason—what subject would not burn with outrage!

sentences.zh: 導門戶小大受國厚恩，今日之事，明目張膽，為六軍之首，寧為忠臣而死，不為無賴而生矣！」

translations.literal: Dao's household, great and small, has received the state's deep grace; in today's affair I stand openly at the head of the six armies—better to die a loyal minister than live a scoundrel!"
translations.idiomatic: Every member of Dao's house has received the state's deepest favor; in this affair I stand openly at the head of the six armies—I would rather die a loyal minister than live as a rogue!"

sentences.zh: 含不答。

translations.literal: Han made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Han did not answer.

sentences.zh: 或以為「王含、錢鳳眾力百倍，苑城小而不固，宜及軍勢未成，大駕自出拒戰」。

translations.literal: Some held that "Wang Han and Qian Feng have forces a hundredfold greater; the park city is small and not secure—it would be best, before their military momentum is formed, for the imperial carriage to go out in person to resist them in battle."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that "Wang Han and Qian Feng commanded forces many times greater, that the park city was small and weak, and that the emperor should lead the army out in person before the rebels could gather their full strength."

sentences.zh: 郗鑒曰：「群逆縱逸，勢不可當，可以謀屈，難以力競。

translations.literal: Xi Jian said, "The rebel host runs riot and their momentum cannot be withstood; they may be subdued by strategy but not by force.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian said, "The rebels are running wild and their momentum cannot be met head-on; they must be overcome by strategy, not brute force.

sentences.zh: 且含等號令不一，抄盜相尋，吏民懲往年暴掠，皆人自為守。

translations.literal: Moreover Han and the others have inconsistent commands and plunder follows plunder; officials and people, chastened by the violent looting of former years, all defend themselves on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han's orders are confused and looting goes on without end; officials and commoners, remembering the pillage of years past, are defending themselves on their own.

sentences.zh: 乘逆順之勢，何憂不克！

translations.literal: Riding the momentum of righteousness against rebellion, why worry that we will not prevail!
translations.idiomatic: With righteousness on our side against rebellion, how can we fail!

sentences.zh: 且賊無經略遠圖，惟恃豕突一戰；

translations.literal: Moreover the rebels have no long-range strategy and rely only on a single boar-like rush;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the rebels have no long-term plan and trust only to one reckless charge;

sentences.zh: 曠日持久，必啟義士之心，令智力得展。

translations.literal: if the days drag on, it will surely awaken the hearts of men of righteousness and allow wisdom and strength to be brought to bear.
translations.idiomatic: if the struggle drags on, loyal hearts will surely rise and wisdom and strength will have room to show themselves.

sentences.zh: 今以此弱力敵彼強寇，決勝負於一朝，定成敗於呼吸。

translations.literal: To pit this weak force against that strong foe and decide victory and defeat in a single morning, fixing success and failure in a breath—
translations.idiomatic: To pit our weak force against their strong band and stake everything on a single morning, deciding success and failure in a breath—

sentences.zh: 萬一蹉跌，雖有申胥之徒，義存投袂，何補於既往哉！」

translations.literal: if we should stumble, even men like Shen Xu who in righteousness would fling aside their sleeves—what good would that do for what is already past!"
translations.idiomatic: if we stumble, even a Shen Xu flinging aside his sleeve in righteous wrath could not undo what was already lost!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held back.

sentences.zh: 帝帥諸軍出屯南皇堂。

translations.literal: The emperor led the armies out to encamp at the Southern Imperial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the armies out to camp at the Southern Imperial Hall.

sentences.zh: 癸酉夜，募壯士，遣將軍段秀、中軍司馬曹渾等帥甲卒千人渡水，掩其未備。

translations.literal: On the night of the day Guiyou he recruited stalwart men and sent General Duan Xiu, Central Army Major Cao Hun, and others to lead a thousand armored soldiers across the water to strike them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on the day Guiyou, he recruited stalwarts and sent General Duan Xiu, Central Army Major Cao Hun, and others with a thousand armored men across the river to take the enemy by surprise.

sentences.zh: 平旦，戰於越城，大破之，斬其前鋒將何康。

translations.literal: At daybreak they fought at Yuecheng, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded their vanguard general He Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought at Yuecheng, routed the enemy, and beheaded the vanguard general He Kang.

sentences.zh: 秀，匹磾之弟也。

translations.literal: Xiu was the younger brother of Murong Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was a younger brother of Murong Pidi.

sentences.zh: 敦聞含敗，大怒曰：「我兄，老婢耳！

translations.literal: When Dun heard that Han had been defeated he raged and said, "My elder brother is but an old serving-woman!
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard of Han's defeat he raged, "My brother is nothing but an old woman!

sentences.zh: 門戶衰。

translations.literal: The clan is in decline.
translations.idiomatic: Our house is ruined.

sentences.zh: 世事去矣！」

translations.literal: The affairs of the age are gone!"
translations.idiomatic: All is lost!"

sentences.zh: 顧謂參軍呂寶曰：「我當力行。」。

translations.literal: He turned to his adjutant Lü Bao and said, "I must exert myself."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his adjutant Lü Bao and said, "I must rouse myself and act."

sentences.zh: 因作勢而起，困乏，復臥，乃謂其舅少府羊鑒及王應曰：「我死，應便即位，先立朝廷百官，然後營葬事。」

translations.literal: He then made a show of rising, but weariness overcame him and he lay down again; he told his maternal uncle, Palace Storehouse Director Yang Jian, and Wang Ying, "When I die, Ying shall immediately take the position; first establish the court's hundred officials, then attend to funeral arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: He made as if to rise, but exhaustion overtook him and he lay down again; he told his uncle Yang Jian, director of the palace storehouse, and Wang Ying, "When I die, Ying is to take command at once—first install the court officials, then see to my burial."

sentences.zh: 敦尋卒，應秘不發喪，裹屍以席，蠟塗其外，埋於廳事中，與諸葛瑤等日夜縱酒淫樂。

translations.literal: Soon after Dun died; Ying kept the death secret, wrapped the corpse in matting, coated the outside with wax, buried it in the reception hall, and with Zhuge Yao and others indulged in wine and debauchery day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Dun soon died; Ying concealed the death, wrapped the body in matting, sealed it with wax, buried it in the main hall, and with Zhuge Yao and others gave himself over to wine and debauchery night and day.

sentences.zh: 帝使吳興沈楨說沈充，許以為司空。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shen Zhen of Wuxing to persuade Shen Chong, promising to make him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shen Zhen of Wuxing to win over Shen Chong with the promise of the post of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 充曰：「三司具瞻之重，豈吾所任！

translations.literal: Chong said, "The weighty dignity of the Three Excellencies looked to by all—how could I bear such an office!
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "The Three Excellencies are the pillars the realm looks to—how could I be fit for such a post!

sentences.zh: 幣厚言甘，古人所畏也。

translations.literal: Rich gifts and sweet words are what the ancients feared.
translations.idiomatic: Rich gifts and honeyed words are what the ancients feared most.

sentences.zh: 且丈夫共事，終始當同，豈可中道改易，人誰容我乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover when men serve together they should stand together from start to finish—how can one change course midway? Who would tolerate me!"
translations.idiomatic: When men serve together they stand together to the end—how can I turn aside halfway? Who would ever trust me again!"

sentences.zh: 遂舉兵趣建康。

translations.literal: He then raised troops and hastened toward Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised troops and marched on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿虞潭以疾歸會稽，聞之，起兵餘姚以討充，帝以潭領會稽內史。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Yu Tan, returning to Kuaiji on account of illness, heard of it and raised troops at Yuyao to attack Chong; the emperor had Tan act as Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan, director of the imperial clan, had returned to Kuaiji on account of illness; when he heard the news he raised troops at Yuyao against Chong, and the emperor appointed him interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 前安東將軍劉超、宣城內史鐘雅皆起兵以討充。

translations.literal: Former Pacifier of the East Liu Chao and Interior Minister of Xuancheng Zhong Ya both raised troops to attack Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Former Pacifier of the East Liu Chao and Interior Minister Zhong Ya of Xuancheng both took up arms against Chong.

sentences.zh: 義興人周蹇殺王敦所署太守劉芳，平西將軍祖約逐敦所署淮南太守任台。

translations.literal: Zhou Jian of Yixing killed Liu Fang, the administrator Wang Dun had appointed; Pacifier of the West Zu Yue drove out Ren Tai, the Huainan administrator Dun had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jian of Yixing killed Liu Fang, the governor Wang Dun had installed; Pacifier of the West Zu Yue drove out Ren Tai, Dun's appointee as Huainan administrator.

sentences.zh: 沈充帥眾萬餘人與王含軍合，司馬顧颺說充曰：「今舉大事，而天子已扼其咽喉，鋒摧氣沮，相持日久，必致禍敗。

translations.literal: Shen Chong led more than ten thousand men to join Han's army; Major Gu Yang said to Chong, "You have launched a great undertaking, yet the Son of Heaven already holds you by the throat; your edge is blunted and your spirit damped—if the standoff drags on, disaster and defeat are sure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong led more than ten thousand men to join Han's forces; Major Gu Yang urged Chong, "You have launched a great rebellion, yet the emperor already has you by the throat; your momentum is spent—if this stalemate drags on, you are doomed.

sentences.zh: 今若決破柵塘，因湖水以灌京邑，乘水勢，縱舟師以攻之，此上策也；

translations.literal: If you now break the sluice dams and use the lake waters to flood the capital, ride the water's force, and unleash the fleet to attack—this is the superior plan;
translations.idiomatic: Break the sluice dams, flood the capital with lake water, and strike by fleet under cover of the flood—that is the high plan;

sentences.zh: 藉初至之銳，並東、西軍之力，十道俱進，眾寡過倍，理必摧陷，中策也；

translations.literal: rely on the sharpness of your newly arrived forces, combine the strength of the eastern and western armies, advance on ten routes at once with numbers more than double theirs—by reason you must crush them—this is the middle plan;
translations.idiomatic: use the edge of your fresh troops, unite the eastern and western armies, advance on ten fronts with more than double their numbers, and crush them by sheer weight—that is the middle plan;

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，召錢鳳計事，因斬之以降，下策也。」

translations.literal: turn misfortune into blessing, summon Qian Feng to consult on affairs, and then behead him to surrender—this is the inferior plan."
translations.idiomatic: turn disaster to advantage by summoning Qian Feng, then killing him and surrendering—that is the low plan."

sentences.zh: 充皆不能用，颺逃歸於吳。

translations.literal: Chong could use none of these; Yang fled back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong would adopt none of them; Yang fled back to Wu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，劉遐、蘇峻等帥精卒萬人至，帝夜見，勞之，賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: On the day Dinghai, Liu Xia, Su Jun, and others arrived leading ten thousand picked soldiers; the emperor received them at night, commended them, and rewarded officers and soldiers each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dinghai, Liu Xia, Su Jun, and others arrived with ten thousand elite troops; the emperor received them by night, praised them, and rewarded the officers and men according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 沈充、錢鳳欲因北軍初到疲睏擊之，乙未夜，充、鳳從竹格渚渡淮。

translations.literal: Shen Chong and Qian Feng wished to strike while the northern army, newly arrived, was weary; on the night of the day Yimao, Chong and Feng crossed the Huai from Zhuge Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong and Qian Feng meant to strike while the northern army was still exhausted from its march; that night, on the day Yimao, they crossed the Huai at Zhuge Ford.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍應詹、建威將軍趙胤等拒戰，不利，充、鳳至宣陽門，拔柵，將戰，劉遐、蘇峻自南塘橫擊，大破之，赴水死者三千人。

translations.literal: Protector-General Ying Zhan, Establishing Might General Zhao Yin, and others resisted but fared ill; Chong and Feng reached the Xuanyang Gate, pulled up the palisades, and were about to give battle when Liu Xia and Su Jun struck across from the Southern Embankment, inflicting a great defeat—three thousand drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Ying Zhan, Establishing Might General Zhao Yin, and others fought but were driven back; Chong and Feng reached the Xuanyang Gate and were pulling up the palisades when Liu Xia and Su Jun struck from the Southern Embankment, routing them—three thousand men drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 遐又破沈充於青溪。

translations.literal: Xia again defeated Shen Chong at Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xia defeated Shen Chong again at Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 尋陽太守周光聞敦舉兵，帥千餘人來赴。

translations.literal: Zhou Guang, Administrator of Xunyang, hearing that Dun had raised troops, led more than a thousand men to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Guang, administrator of Xunyang, heard that Dun had risen in arms, he led more than a thousand men to join him.

sentences.zh: 既至，求見敦。

translations.literal: When he arrived he asked to see Dun.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he asked to see Dun.

sentences.zh: 王應辭以疾。

translations.literal: Wang Ying excused Dun on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying pleaded illness on Dun's behalf.

sentences.zh: 光退曰：「今我遠來而不得見，公其死乎！」

translations.literal: Guang withdrew, saying, "I have come from afar and cannot see him—the master must be dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang withdrew, saying, "I have come all this way and cannot see him—he must be dead!"

sentences.zh: 遽見其兄撫曰：「王公已死，兄何為與錢鳳作賊！」

translations.literal: He hurried to see his elder brother Fu and said, "Lord Wang is already dead—elder brother, why do you join Qian Feng in becoming a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to his brother Fu and cried, "Lord Wang is dead—brother, why do you make common cause with Qian Feng the rebel!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆愕然。

translations.literal: All were stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was stunned.

sentences.zh: 丙申，王含等燒營夜遁。

translations.literal: On the day Bingshen, Wang Han and the others burned their camp and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingshen, Wang Han and his men burned their camp and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，帝還宮，大赦，惟敦黨不原。

translations.literal: On the day Dingyou the emperor returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and excepted only Dun's faction from pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingyou the emperor returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and pardoned all except Dun's faction.

sentences.zh: 命庾亮督蘇峻等追沈充於吳興，溫嶠督劉遐等追王含、錢鳳於江寧，分命諸將追其黨與。

translations.literal: He ordered Yu Liang to direct Su Jun and others in pursuing Shen Chong in Wuxing, and Wen Jiao to direct Liu Xia and others in pursuing Wang Han and Qian Feng at Jiangning; he separately commanded the generals to pursue their partisans.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yu Liang, with Su Jun and others, to pursue Shen Chong in Wuxing, and Wen Jiao, with Liu Xia and others, to pursue Wang Han and Qian Feng at Jiangning; other generals were sent after the remaining conspirators.

sentences.zh: 劉遐軍人頗縱虜掠，嶠責之曰：「天道助順，故王含剿絕，豈可因亂為亂也！」

translations.literal: Liu Xia's soldiers rather freely plundered captives; Jiao rebuked him, saying, "Heaven's way aids the righteous, and therefore Wang Han has been destroyed—how can you make chaos out of chaos!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia's men plundered freely; Jiao rebuked him: "Heaven aids the righteous, and that is why Wang Han has been destroyed—will you now add chaos to chaos!"

sentences.zh: 遐惶恐拜謝。

translations.literal: Xia, in fear and trembling, bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xia bowed in fear and apologized.

sentences.zh: 王含欲奔荊州，王應曰：「不如江州。」

translations.literal: Wang Han wished to flee to Jingzhou; Wang Ying said, "Better to go to Jiangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han wanted to flee to Jingzhou; Wang Ying said, "Jiangzhou would be better."

sentences.zh: 含曰：「大將軍平素與江州雲何，而欲歸之？」

translations.literal: Han said, "What were the Grand General's usual relations with Jiangzhou, that you wish to go there?"
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "What were the Grand General's relations with Jiangzhou, that you would go there?"

sentences.zh: 應曰：「此乃所以宜歸也。

translations.literal: Ying said, "That is precisely why we ought to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied, "That is exactly why we should go there.

sentences.zh: 江州當人強盛時，能立同異，此非常人所及，今睹困厄，必有愍惻之心。

translations.literal: When Jiangzhou was at its strongest it could stand apart with its own views—this is beyond ordinary men; now that it sees us in distress, it is sure to feel compassion.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangzhou was strong it dared stand apart from us—few could do that; now that it sees us in distress, it will surely pity us.

sentences.zh: 荊州守文，豈能意外行事邪！」

translations.literal: Jingzhou adheres to the letter of the law—how could it act outside the expected!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou clings to the letter of the law—it would never act outside convention!"

sentences.zh: 含不從，遂奔荊州。

translations.literal: Han would not follow this and fled to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han refused and fled to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王舒遣軍迎之，沉含父子於江。

translations.literal: Wang Shu sent troops to meet them and drowned Han and his son in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu sent troops to meet them and drowned Han and his son in the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 王彬聞應當來，密具舟以侍之；

translations.literal: Wang Bin, hearing that Ying was likely to come, secretly prepared boats to await him;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin, hearing that Ying might come to him, secretly prepared boats to receive him;

sentences.zh: 不至，深以為恨。

translations.literal: when he did not arrive, Bin deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: when Ying never came, he was deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 錢鳳走至闔廬洲，周光斬之，詣闕自贖。

translations.literal: Qian Feng fled to Helu Isle; Zhou Guang beheaded him and went to the palace to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng fled to Helu Isle; Zhou Guang beheaded him and presented himself at court to atone for his earlier loyalty to Dun.

sentences.zh: 沈充走失道，誤入故將吳儒家。

translations.literal: Shen Chong, having lost his way, strayed into the home of his former officer Wu Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, having lost his way, blundered into the house of his former officer Wu Ru.

sentences.zh: 儒誘充內重壁中，因笑謂充曰：「三千戶侯矣！」

translations.literal: Ru lured Chong inside a double wall and, laughing, said to him, "A marquisate of three thousand households!"
translations.idiomatic: Ru lured him into a hidden chamber and laughed, "A marquisate of three thousand households is yours!"

sentences.zh: 充曰：「爾以義存我，我家必厚報汝。

translations.literal: Chong said, "If you preserve me out of righteousness, my family will surely reward you richly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "If you spare me out of loyalty, my family will reward you handsomely.

sentences.zh: 若以利殺我，我死，汝族滅矣。」

translations.literal: If you kill me for profit, when I die your clan will be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: If you kill me for gain, when I die your whole clan will perish."

sentences.zh: 儒遂殺之，傳首建康。

translations.literal: Ru then killed him and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Ru killed him anyway and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 敦黨悉平。

translations.literal: Dun's faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's faction was wholly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 充子勁當坐誅，鄉人錢舉匿之，得免；

translations.literal: Chong's son Jin was due for execution; his fellow townsman Qian Ju hid him and he escaped death;
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son Jin was condemned to death; a townsman named Qian Ju hid him and he escaped execution;

sentences.zh: 其後勁竟滅吳氏。

translations.literal: later Jin in the end exterminated the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: in the end Jin wiped out the Wu family.

sentences.zh: 有司發王敦瘞，出屍，焚其衣冠，跽而斬之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials opened Wang Dun's tomb, removed the corpse, burned his robes and cap, and beheaded him while kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities opened Wang Dun's tomb, took out the corpse, burned his robes, and beheaded the body in formal kneeling posture.

sentences.zh: 與沈充首同懸於南桁。

translations.literal: His head was hung together with Shen Chong's on the southern bridge.
translations.idiomatic: His head was displayed alongside Shen Chong's on the southern bridge.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒言於帝曰：「前朝誅楊駿等，皆先極官刑，後聽私殯。

translations.literal: Xi Jian said to the emperor, "In the previous reign, when Yang Jun and others were executed, they were first subjected to the full official punishment and only afterward allowed private burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian told the emperor, "When Yang Jun and his faction were executed in the previous reign, they were first subjected to full official punishment and only afterward allowed private burial.

sentences.zh: 臣以為王誅加於上，私義行於下，宜聽敦家收葬，於義為弘。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that when royal punishment is imposed from above and private duty is exercised below, Dun's family should be allowed to gather and bury him—this would be magnanimous in principle."
translations.idiomatic: I believe that when the throne has exacted its punishment, private duty may still be fulfilled below; Dun's family should be allowed to bury him—this would be the magnanimous course."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 司徒導等皆以討敦功受封賞。

translations.literal: Minister Dao and others all received enfeoffments and rewards for their merit in punishing Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dao and others were all enfeoffed and rewarded for their service against Dun.

sentences.zh: 周撫與鄧岳俱亡，周光欲資給其兄而取岳。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu and Deng Yue were both in flight; Zhou Guang wished to supply his elder brother and seize Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu and Deng Yue were both fugitives; Zhou Guang meant to supply his brother and capture Yue.

sentences.zh: 撫怒曰：「我與伯山同亡，何不先斬我！」

translations.literal: Fu raged and said, "Boshan and I will perish together—why not behead me first!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu raged, "Boshan and I will live or die together—why not strike me down first!"

sentences.zh: 會岳至，撫出門遙謂之曰：「何不速去！

translations.literal: When Yue arrived, Fu went to the gate and called to him from afar, "Why do you not flee at once!
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived, Fu went to the gate and shouted to him from afar, "Why do you not flee at once!

sentences.zh: 今骨肉尚欲相危，況他人乎！」

translations.literal: If even flesh and blood now seek to endanger one another, what of others!"
translations.idiomatic: If even kin turn on one another, what hope is there for anyone else!"

sentences.zh: 岳回舟而走，與撫共入西陽蠻中。

translations.literal: Yue turned his boat and fled; together with Fu he entered the Xiyang barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yue turned his boat about and fled; he and Fu took refuge among the Xiyang tribes.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔原敦黨，撫、岳出首，得免死禁錮。

translations.literal: The next year an edict pardoned Dun's faction; Fu and Yue came forward and were spared death, receiving imprisonment instead.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict pardoned Dun's followers; Fu and Yue surrendered and were spared death, though imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 故吳內史張茂妻陸氏，傾家產，帥茂部曲為先登以討沈充，報其夫仇。

translations.literal: Lu, wife of the former Interior Minister of Wu Zhang Mao, exhausted her family's property, led Mao's personal troops as the first to scale the walls in attacking Shen Chong, and avenged her husband.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of the late Interior Minister Zhang Mao of Wu, spent her family's entire fortune, led her husband's retainers as the first over the wall against Shen Chong, and avenged her husband's death.

sentences.zh: 充敗，陸氏詣闕上書，為茂謝不克之責；

translations.literal: When Chong was defeated, Lady Lu went to the palace and submitted a memorial apologizing on Mao's behalf for his failure to prevail;
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's defeat, Lady Lu went to court and submitted a memorial apologizing on Mao's behalf for his failure to hold out;

sentences.zh: 詔贈茂太僕。

translations.literal: an edict posthumously conferred on Mao the title of Grand Servant.
translations.idiomatic: the throne posthumously honored Mao as grand servant.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「王彬等敦之親族，皆當除名。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized, "Wang Bin and others, kinsmen of Dun, should all be struck from the registers."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities memorialized that Wang Bin and other kinsmen of Dun should all be struck from the registers."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司徒導以大義滅親，猶將百世宥之，況彬等皆公之近親乎！」

translations.literal: An edict said, "Minister Dao destroyed his own kin for the sake of righteousness, yet he is still to be pardoned for a hundred generations—how much more Bin and the others, who are all the Duke's close kin!"
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "Minister Dao destroyed his own kin for righteousness' sake, yet he is still to be pardoned for generations—how much more Bin and the others, who are the Duke's own close kin!"

sentences.zh: 悉無所問。

translations.literal: None were questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: None were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「王敦綱紀除名，參佐禁錮」溫嶠上疏曰：「王敦剛愎不仁，忍行殺戮，朝廷所不能制，骨肉所不能諫；

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Strike Wang Dun's name from the statutes and imprison his staff." Wen Jiao submitted a memorial, saying, "Wang Dun was obstinate, cruel, and without benevolence, ruthless in killing; the court could not restrain him and his own kin could not remonstrate with him;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Dun's name struck from the statutes and his staff imprisoned. Wen Jiao memorialized: "Wang Dun was obstinate, cruel, and merciless; the court could not restrain him and even his kin could not dissuade him;

sentences.zh: 處其朝者，恆懼危亡，故人士結舌，道路以目，誠賢人君子道窮數盡，遵養時晦之辰也。

translations.literal: those who served in his court constantly feared ruin and death, so gentlemen sealed their tongues and men communicated by glances in the streets—it was truly the time when worthy men and gentlemen, their Way exhausted and their fate spent, observed the precept of nurturing their virtue and biding their time in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: those who served in his court lived in constant fear for their lives; men of talent fell silent and exchanged glances in the streets—it was the hour when worthy men, their path blocked and their fate spent, could only nurture virtue and bide their time in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 原其私心，豈遑晏處！

translations.literal: If one examines their private hearts, how could they have leisure to dwell at ease!
translations.idiomatic: If one considers what was in their hearts, how could they have lived at ease!

sentences.zh: 如陸玩、劉胤、郭璞之徒常與臣言，備知之矣。

translations.literal: Men such as Lu Wan, Liu Yin, and Guo Pu often spoke with your servant—I know this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Lu Wan, Liu Yin, and Guo Pu often spoke with me of this—I know it well.

sentences.zh: 必其贊導凶悖，自當正以典刑；

translations.literal: if they truly aided and guided his vicious rebellion, they should naturally be punished according to the statutes;
translations.idiomatic: If they truly abetted his wicked rebellion, they should be punished under the law;

sentences.zh: 如其枉陷奸黨，謂宜施之寬貸。

translations.literal: if they were wrongly charged as members of a treacherous faction, I hold that leniency should be shown them.
translations.idiomatic: If they were falsely accused as conspirators, they deserve clemency.

sentences.zh: 臣以玩等之誠，聞於聖聽，當受同賊之責；

translations.literal: your servant, having reported Wan and the others' sincerity to the sacred ear, ought to bear the same responsibility as traitors;
translations.idiomatic: Since I have brought Lu Wan and the others' loyalty to Your Majesty's attention, I should share their guilt if I am wrong;

sentences.zh: 苟默而不言，實負其心，惟陛下仁聖裁之！」

translations.literal: if I were to keep silent, I would truly betray my heart—may Your Majesty, in your benevolence and sagacity, decide!"
translations.idiomatic: To remain silent would betray my conscience. I entrust the matter to Your Majesty's wise judgment!"

sentences.zh: 郗鑒以為先王立君臣之教，貴於伏節死義。

translations.literal: Xi Jian held that in establishing the teaching between ruler and minister, former kings valued preserving integrity and dying for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian argued that earlier kings, in teaching the bonds of lord and subject, prized loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 王敦佐吏，雖多逼迫，然進不能止其逆謀，退不能脫身遠遁，准之前訓，宜加義責。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's staff, though largely under coercion, could neither advance to stop his rebellious design nor retreat to escape far away; measured against earlier instruction, they deserved censure for failing their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Though many of Wang Dun's subordinates acted under duress, none could check his rebellion or flee to safety; by the standards of old, they failed their duty and deserved condemnation.

sentences.zh: 帝卒從嶠議。

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed Jiao's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately adopted Jiao's view.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以司徒導為太保、領司徒，加殊禮，西陽王羕領太尉，應詹為江州刺史，劉遐為徐州刺史，代王邃鎮淮陰，蘇峻為歷陽內史，加庾亮護軍將軍，溫嶠前將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister Dao was made Grand Tutor while retaining the post of Minister, with extraordinary honors; Prince of Xiyang Yi was given charge of the Grand Commandant; Ying Zhan was made Inspector of Jiangzhou; Liu Xia was made Inspector of Xuzhou, replacing Wang Sui in garrison at Huaiyin; Su Jun was made Interior Administrator of Liyang; Yu Liang was promoted to Protector-General; and Wen Jiao to Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Minister Dao was named Grand Tutor while keeping the ministry, with extraordinary honors; Prince Yi of Xiyang took the grand commandantship; Ying Zhan became inspector of Jiangzhou; Liu Xia became inspector of Xuzhou, replacing Wang Sui at Huaiyin; Su Jun was made interior administrator of Liyang; Yu Liang was promoted to protector-general; and Wen Jiao to forward general.

sentences.zh: 導固辭不受。

translations.literal: Dao firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Dao repeatedly declined and refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 應詹至江州，吏民未安，詹撫而懷之，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: When Ying Zhan arrived at Jiangzhou, officials and people were still unsettled; Zhan soothed and embraced them, and none failed to submit gladly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying Zhan reached Jiangzhou, the officials and populace were still uneasy; he reassured them with kindness until all submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 十二月，涼州將辛晏據枹罕，不服，張駿將討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzhou general Xin Yan held Fuhan in defiance; Zhang Jun was about to march against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the Liangzhou general Xin Yan seized Fuhan and refused obedience; Zhang Jun prepared to attack him.

sentences.zh: 從事劉慶諫曰：「霸王之師，必須天時、人事相得，然後乃起。

translations.literal: Attendant Liu Qing remonstrated, saying, "An army of hegemony must have Heaven's season and human affairs align before it can be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Liu Qing admonished him: "A conquering army requires the right season and popular support alike before it can be dispatched.

sentences.zh: 辛晏凶狂安忍，其亡可必；

translations.literal: Xin Yan is fierce, reckless, and cruel—his fall is certain;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yan is brutal and savage—his defeat is inevitable;

sentences.zh: 標何以饑年大舉，盛寒攻城乎！」

translations.literal: why, my lord, launch a major campaign in a famine year and storm a city in bitter cold!"
translations.idiomatic: Why would you, my lord, mount a major campaign in a year of famine and lay siege in the dead of winter!"

sentences.zh: 駿乃止。

translations.literal: Jun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun desisted.

sentences.zh: 駿遣參軍王騭聘於趙，趙主曜謂之曰：「貴州款誠和好，卿能保之乎？」

translations.literal: Jun sent aide Wang Bi on a mission to Zhao; Zhao's ruler Yao said to him, "Your province has come forward in sincerity and friendship—can you guarantee this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sent his aide Wang Bi to Zhao on a diplomatic mission. Zhao's ruler Liu Yao asked him, "Your province professes goodwill—can you guarantee it will last?"

sentences.zh: 騭曰：「不能。」

translations.literal: Bi said, "I cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi replied, "No, I cannot."

sentences.zh: 侍中徐邈曰：「君來結好，而雲不能保，何也？」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Miao said, "You came to forge friendship, yet say you cannot guarantee it—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Xu Miao asked, "You came to make peace, yet say you cannot guarantee it—why?"

sentences.zh: 騭曰：「齊桓貫澤之盟，憂心兢兢，諸侯不召自至；

translations.literal: Bi said, "At Duke Huan of Qi's covenant at Guanze, he was anxious and trembling with care, and the feudal lords came without being summoned;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi said, "At Duke Huan of Qi's Guanze covenant, he was anxious and vigilant, and the feudal lords came unbidden;

sentences.zh: 葵丘之會，振而矜之，叛者九國。

translations.literal: at the meeting at Kuiqiu, he grew arrogant and self-important, and nine states rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuiqiu he grew arrogant, and nine states turned against him.

sentences.zh: 趙國之化，常如今日，可也；

translations.literal: If Zhao's transformation remains as it is today, that is acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao's governance stays as virtuous as it is today, that will suffice;

sentences.zh: 若政教陵遲，尚未能察邇者之變，況鄙州乎！」

translations.literal: but if government and teaching decline, you will not yet be able to detect changes in those near at hand—how much less in our humble province!"
translations.idiomatic: But if your rule falters, you may fail to see trouble even on your doorstep—how much less in our distant province!"

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「此涼州之君子也，擇使可謂得人矣！」

translations.literal: Yao said, "This is a gentleman of Liangzhou—one may say the choice of envoy was well made!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "This is a true gentleman of Liangzhou—you chose your envoy well!"

sentences.zh: 厚禮而遣之。

translations.literal: He honored him generously and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao treated him generously and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，代王賀辱始親國政，以諸部多未服，乃築城於東木根山，徙居之。

translations.literal: That year, Dai King Helu began personally to administer state affairs; because many of the tribes were still unsubmissive, he built a city at Dongmugen Mountain and moved his seat there.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Dai king Tuoba Helu took personal charge of government; since many tribal groups remained rebellious, he built a city on Mount Dongmugen and moved his capital there.

sentences.zh: 肅宗明皇帝下太寧三年（

translations.literal: Under the chronicle of the Illustrious Ancestor, Emperor Ming—the third year of Taining (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, third year of Taining (

sentences.zh: 乙酉、公元三二五年）

translations.literal: Yiyou, corresponding to the year 325 CE)
translations.idiomatic: year Yiyou, AD 325)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，張駿承元帝凶問，大臨三日。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Zhang Jun, upon receiving word of Emperor Yuan's death, performed the great mourning rites for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, Zhang Jun learned of Emperor Yuan's death and observed three days of full mourning.

sentences.zh: 會黃龍見嘉泉，汜禕等請改年以章休祥，駿不許。

translations.literal: When a yellow dragon appeared at Jiaquan, Si Yi and others asked to change the reign era to proclaim the auspicious omen; Jun did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow dragon was sighted at Jiaquan; Si Yi and others petitioned to change the reign year to mark the auspicious sign, but Zhang Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 辛晏以枹罕降，駿復收河南之地。

translations.literal: Xin Yan surrendered Fuhan; Jun recovered the lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yan surrendered Fuhan, and Zhang Jun regained the territory south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 贈故譙王承、甘卓、戴淵、周顗、虞望、郭璞、王澄等官。

translations.literal: Posthumous offices were granted to the late Prince Qiao Cheng, Gan Zhuo, Dai Yuan, Zhou Yi, Yu Wang, Guo Pu, Wang Cheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous offices were conferred on the late Prince Qiao Cheng, Gan Zhuo, Dai Yuan, Zhou Yi, Yu Wang, Guo Pu, Wang Cheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 周札故吏為札訟冤，尚書卞壺議，以為：「札守石頭，開門延寇，不當贈謚。」

translations.literal: Former retainers of Zhou Zha pleaded Zha's innocence; Minister Bian Hu argued that "Zha held Stone City and opened the gates to invite the enemy—he should not receive a posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: Former retainers of Zhou Zha petitioned on his behalf; Minister Bian Hu argued that Zhou Zha had held Stone City and opened its gates to the enemy and therefore deserved no posthumous title."

sentences.zh: 司徒導以為：「往年之事，敦奸逆未彰，自臣等有識以上，皆所未悟，與札無異；

translations.literal: Minister Dao held that "in the events of former years, Dun's treachery had not yet been revealed; from those of understanding among us ministers upward, none had perceived it—we were no different from Zha;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dao countered that "when those events occurred, Dun's treason was not yet apparent; none of us who should have known better saw through him—we were no different from Zhou Zha;

sentences.zh: 既悟其奸，札便以身許國，尋取梟夷。

translations.literal: once his treachery was known, Zha then pledged his body to the state and was soon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dun's treachery was exposed, Zhou Zha gave his life for the realm and was soon put to death.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜與周、戴同例。」

translations.literal: your servant holds that he should be treated the same as Zhou and Dai."
translations.idiomatic: I hold he should receive the same honors as Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan."

sentences.zh: 郗鑒以為：「周、戴死節，周札延寇，事異賞均，何以勸沮！

translations.literal: Xi Jian held that "Zhou and Dai died for principle, while Zhou Zha welcomed the enemy—the deeds differ, yet the reward would be the same; how would one encourage loyalty or deter treachery!
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian objected: "Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan died loyal deaths, while Zhou Zha let the enemy in—the cases differ, yet you would reward them alike. How would that encourage virtue or punish betrayal?

sentences.zh: 如司徒議，謂往年有識以上皆與札無異，則譙王、周、戴皆應受責，何贈謚之有！

translations.literal: If, as the Minister argues, all the understanding ones of former years were no different from Zha, then Prince Qiao, Zhou, and Dai should all bear censure—what posthumous titles could there be!
translations.idiomatic: If, as Minister Dao says, none of us who should have known better differed from Zhou Zha, then Prince Qiao, Zhou Yi, and Dai Yuan should all be condemned—what posthumous honors could they deserve?

sentences.zh: 今三臣既褒，則札宜受貶明矣。」

translations.literal: Now that the three ministers have already been honored, Zha clearly ought to be disgraced."
translations.idiomatic: Since those three have already been honored, Zhou Zha should clearly be marked down instead."

sentences.zh: 導曰：「札與譙王、周、戴，雖所見有異同，皆人臣之節也。」

translations.literal: Dao said, "Zha, Prince Qiao, Zhou, and Dai, though their courses differed, all fulfilled a minister's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dao replied, "Zhou Zha, Prince Qiao, Zhou Yi, and Dai Yuan acted differently, yet each upheld a minister's duty in his own way."

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「敦之逆謀，履霜日久，緣札開門，令王師不振。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Dun's rebellious design had been building like frost over a long time; because Zha opened the gates, the royal army lost its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian rejoined, "Dun's rebellion had been gathering for years; because Zhou Zha opened the gates, the imperial forces were broken.

sentences.zh: 若敦前者之舉，義同桓、文，則先帝可為幽、厲邪！」

translations.literal: If Dun's earlier action had the righteousness of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, then could the late emperor be regarded as King You or King Li!"
translations.idiomatic: If Dun's revolt was as righteous as the deeds of Duke Huan or Duke Wen, are we to call the late emperor a tyrant like You or Li of Zhou!"

sentences.zh: 然卒用導議，贈札衛尉。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Dao's opinion prevailed, and Zha was posthumously given the office of Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor followed Minister Dao's view and posthumously made Zhou Zha Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒加宇文乞得歸官爵，使之擊慕容廆。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le restored Qidegui's office and nobility and had him attack Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's Shi Le restored Qidegui's rank and title and sent him to attack Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 廆遣世子皝、索頭、段國共擊之，以遼東相裴嶷為右翼，慕容仁為左翼。

translations.literal: Hui sent his heir Huans, Suotou, and Duan Guo to attack him jointly, with Liaodong Chancellor Pei Ni on the right wing and Murong Ren on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui sent his heir Huans, Suotou, and Duan Guo against him, with Liaodong chancellor Pei Ni commanding the right and Murong Ren the left.

sentences.zh: 乞得歸據澆水以拒皝，遣兄子悉拔雄拒仁。

translations.literal: Qidegui held the Jiao River to resist Huans and sent his brother's son Xibaxiong to oppose Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Qidegui held the Jiao River against Huans and sent his nephew Xibaxiong to block Murong Ren.

sentences.zh: 仁擊悉拔雄，斬之；

translations.literal: Ren attacked Xibaxiong and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ren struck Xibaxiong and killed him;

sentences.zh: 乘勝與皝攻乞得歸，大破之。

translations.literal: pressing the victory, he joined Huans in attacking Qidegui and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Then he pressed the advantage with Huans and routed Qidegui.

sentences.zh: 乞得歸棄軍走，皝、仁進入其國城，使輕兵追乞得歸，過其國三百餘里而還，盡獲其國重器，畜產以百萬計，民之降附者數萬。

translations.literal: Qidegui abandoned his army and fled; Huans and Ren entered his capital, sent light troops in pursuit over three hundred li into his territory and then returned, and seized all the state's treasures; livestock numbered in the millions, and tens of thousands of people submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qidegui fled with his army in disarray. Huans and Ren occupied his capital, sent light cavalry in pursuit more than three hundred li into his territory, and withdrew with every treasure of the realm, livestock numbering in the millions, and tens of thousands of people who submitted.

sentences.zh: 三月，段末柸卒，弟牙立。

translations.literal: In the third month, Duan Moben died; his younger brother Ya succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Duan Moben died, and his younger brother Ya succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，立皇子衍為太子，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen, the emperor's son Yan was established as crown prince, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen, Prince Yan was enthroned as crown prince and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜立皇后劉氏。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Yao installed the Lady Liu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao of Zhao made Lady Liu his empress.

sentences.zh: 北羌王盆句除附於趙，後趙將石佗自雁門出上郡襲之，俘三千落，獲牛、馬、羊百餘萬而歸。

translations.literal: Pen Juchu, king of the Northern Qiang, submitted to Zhao; Later Zhao general Shi Tuo marched from Yanmen through Shangjun to attack him, captured three thousand households, and returned with more than a million head of cattle, horses, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Pen Juchu, king of the Northern Qiang, submitted to Zhao. Later Zhao general Shi Tuo sortied from Yanmen through Shangcommandery, captured three thousand tribes, and returned with more than a million head of cattle, horses, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜遣中山王岳追之，曜屯於富平，為岳聲援。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Yao sent Prince of Zhongshan Yue in pursuit; Yao encamped at Fuping to lend Yue support.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Prince Yue of Zhongshan in pursuit and encamped at Fuping to support him.

sentences.zh: 岳與石佗戰於河濱，斬之，後趙兵死者六千餘人，岳悉收所虜而歸。

translations.literal: Yue fought Shi Tuo on the riverbank, beheaded him, and more than six thousand Later Zhao soldiers died; Yue recovered all the captives and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fought Shi Tuo on the riverbank, killed him, and slew more than six thousand Later Zhao troops, then recovered all the captives and returned.

sentences.zh: 楊難敵襲仇池，克之，執田崧，立之於前，左右令崧拜。

translations.literal: Yang Nanadi attacked Chou and took it; he seized Tian Song, set him before him, and had his attendants order Song to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nanadi assaulted Chou Pool and captured it. He seized Tian Song, brought him forward, and ordered his attendants to make him bow.
