sentences.zh: 崧瞋目叱之曰：「氐狗！

translations.literal: Song glared and shouted at him, "Di cur!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Song glared and shouted, "You Di cur!

sentences.zh: 安有天子牧伯而向賊拜乎！」

translations.literal: How can there be an imperial inspector who bows to a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: What imperial inspector would bow to a bandit!"

sentences.zh: 難敵字謂之曰：「子岱，吾當與子共定大業，子忠於劉氏，豈不能忠於我乎！」

translations.literal: Nanadi addressed him by his style, saying, "Master Dai, I intend to establish great undertakings with you; you were loyal to the Liu house—can you not be loyal to me as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nanadi addressed him familiarly: "Master Dai, I mean to build a great enterprise with you. You were loyal to the Liu house—why not be loyal to me?"

sentences.zh: 崧厲色大言曰：「賊氐，汝本奴才，何謂大業！

translations.literal: Song, with stern countenance, spoke loudly: "Bandit Di, you were originally a slave—what talk of great undertakings!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Song answered fiercely: "Bandit of the Di, you were born a slave—what great enterprise!

sentences.zh: 我寧為趙鬼，不為汝臣！」

translations.literal: I would rather be a ghost of Zhao than your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather be a ghost in Zhao than your subject!"

sentences.zh: 顧排一人，奪其劍，前刺難敵，不中，難敵殺之。

translations.literal: He shoved a man aside, seized his sword, and thrust at Nanadi but missed; Nanadi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He shoved a man aside, snatched his sword, and lunged at Yang Nanadi but missed; Yang Nanadi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 都尉魯潛以許昌叛，降於後趙。

translations.literal: Commandant Lu Qian rebelled at Xuchang and surrendered to Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Lu Qian rebelled at Xuchang and defected to Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，後趙將石瞻攻兗州刺史檀斌於鄒山，殺之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Zhan attacked Tan Bin, Inspector of Yanzhou, at Zou Mountain and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Zhan attacked Yanzhou inspector Tan Bin at Mount Zou and killed him.

sentences.zh: 後趙西夷中郎將王騰襲殺并州刺史崔琨、上黨內史王慎據并州降趙。

translations.literal: Later Zhao General of the Western Barbarians Wang Teng launched a surprise attack and killed Inspector of Bingzhou Cui Kun; Interior Administrator of Shangdang Wang Shen held Bingzhou and surrendered to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's general of the western barbarians Wang Teng ambushed and killed Bingzhou inspector Cui Kun; Shangdang interior administrator Wang Shen seized Bingzhou and surrendered to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 五月，以陶侃為征西大將軍、都督荊、湘、雍、梁四州諸軍事、荊州刺史，荊州士女相慶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Tao Kan was made Grand General Who Conquers the West, commander of all military affairs in the four provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, and Liang, and Inspector of Jingzhou; the gentlemen and women of Jingzhou rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Tao Kan was appointed grand general who conquers the west, commander of Jing, Xiang, Yong, and Liang, and inspector of Jingzhou; the people of Jingzhou celebrated together.

sentences.zh: 侃性聰敏恭勤，終日斂膝危坐，軍府眾事，檢攝無遺，未嘗少閒。

translations.literal: Kan was intelligent, respectful, and diligent; all day he sat upright with knees drawn in; in the army headquarters he oversaw every matter without omission and was never idle even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was quick-witted, respectful, and tireless; he sat upright all day long, overseeing every detail of headquarters business without a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「大禹聖人，乃惜寸陰；

translations.literal: He often told others, "Yu the Great was a sage, yet he cherished every inch of shadow;
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Yu the Great was a sage, yet he treasured every inch of daylight;

sentences.zh: 至於眾人，當惜分陰，豈可但逸游荒醉！

translations.literal: as for ordinary men, they should cherish every fraction of shadow—how can they simply wander in idleness and waste themselves in drunkenness!
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest of us, we should treasure every fraction of an hour—how can we simply idle away our days in pleasure and drunkenness!

sentences.zh: 生無益於時，死無聞於後，是自棄也！」

translations.literal: To live without benefit to the age and die without leaving a name behind is to abandon oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: To live without serving the age and die without leaving a name is to throw one's life away!"

sentences.zh: 諸參佐或以談戲廢事者，命取其酒器、蒲博之具，悉投之於江，將吏則加鞭撲，曰：「樗蒲者，牧豬奴戲耳！

translations.literal: When any staff member neglected duty for idle talk or games, he had their wine vessels and dice-casting implements taken and all thrown into the river; officers and clerks were flogged, and he said, "Dice games are the sport of swineherds!
translations.idiomatic: When aides neglected their duties for idle chatter or games, he had their wine cups and dice thrown into the river and had officers flogged, saying, "Dice games are the pastime of swineherds!

sentences.zh: 老、莊浮華，非先王之法言，不益實用。

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi are ornate flourishes—not the authoritative words of former kings, and of no practical benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The writings of Laozi and Zhuangzi are elegant but empty—not the authoritative teachings of the ancient kings, and of no practical use.

sentences.zh: 君子當正其威儀，何有蓬頭跣足，自謂宏達耶！」

translations.literal: A gentleman should keep his dignity correct—what business is there in going with disheveled hair and bare feet and calling oneself broad-minded!"
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman should maintain proper bearing—what virtue is there in going disheveled and barefoot and calling oneself broad-minded!"

sentences.zh: 有奉饋者，必問其所由，若力作所致，雖微必喜，慰賜參倍；

translations.literal: When anyone brought a gift, he always asked its source; if it came from honest labor, however small, he was pleased and rewarded the giver several times over;
translations.idiomatic: When anyone brought him a gift, he always asked where it came from; if it was earned by hard work, however modest, he was delighted and rewarded the giver several times over;

sentences.zh: 若非理得之，則切厲訶辱，還其所饋。

translations.literal: if it was obtained unreasonably, he sternly rebuked and insulted the giver and returned the gift.
translations.idiomatic: If it was obtained improperly, he scolded the giver harshly and sent the gift back.

sentences.zh: 嘗出遊，見人持一把未熟稻，侃問：「用此何為？」

translations.literal: Once when he went out on an inspection tour, he saw a man holding a handful of unripe rice; Kan asked, "What is this for?"
translations.idiomatic: Once on an inspection tour he saw a man carrying a handful of unripe rice. Tao Kan asked, "What is that for?"

sentences.zh: 人云：「行道所見，聊取之耳。」

translations.literal: The man said, "I saw it along the road and took it on a whim."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied, "I saw it along the road and picked it up on a whim."

sentences.zh: 侃大怒曰：「汝既不佃，而戲賊人稻！」

translations.literal: Kan flew into a rage and said, "You do not farm, yet you trifle with and steal another man's rice!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan flew into a rage: "You do not farm, yet you treat another man's rice as a toy!"

sentences.zh: 執而鞭之。

translations.literal: He had him seized and flogged.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man seized and flogged.

sentences.zh: 是以百姓勤於農作，家給人足。

translations.literal: Because of this the common people were diligent in farming, and every household was supplied and every person had enough.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the people worked hard at farming, and households prospered.

sentences.zh: 嘗造船，其木屑竹頭，侃皆令籍而掌之，人鹹不解所以。

translations.literal: Once when ships were being built, he had all the wood shavings and bamboo ends registered and stored; everyone wondered why.
translations.idiomatic: When ships were being built, he had every wood shaving and bamboo end collected and stored, to everyone's puzzlement.

sentences.zh: 後正會，積雪始晴，聽事前餘雪猶濕，乃以木屑布地。

translations.literal: Later, during a formal assembly, snow had just cleared and the ground before the hall was still wet from melted snow; he spread the wood shavings on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a formal assembly after snow had cleared, the ground before the hall was still wet; he spread the wood shavings to dry it.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫伐蜀，又以侃所貯竹頭作丁裝船。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen marched against Shu, the bamboo ends Kan had stored were also used as pegs to fit out ships.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen campaigned against Shu, Tao Kan's hoarded bamboo ends were used as pegs to assemble ships.

sentences.zh: 其綜理微密，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His comprehensive management in minute detail was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His meticulous attention to detail showed in countless ways like these.

sentences.zh: 後趙將石生屯洛陽，寇掠河南，司州刺史李矩、穎川太守郭默軍數敗，又乏食，乃遣使附於趙。

translations.literal: Later Zhao general Shi Sheng encamped at Luoyang and raided Henan; Inspector of Sizhou Li Ju and Administrator of Yingchuan Guo Mo suffered repeated defeats and also lacked food, so they sent envoys to submit to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao general Shi Sheng held Luoyang and raided Henan. Sizhou inspector Li Ju and Yingchuan administrator Guo Mo were repeatedly defeated and ran short of food, so they sent envoys to submit to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜使中山王岳將兵萬五千人趣孟津，鎮東將軍呼延謨帥荊、司之眾自崤、澠而東，欲會矩、默共攻石生。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Yao sent Prince of Zhongshan Yue with fifteen thousand troops to advance on Mengjin; General Who Guards the East Huyan Mo led the forces of Jing and Si eastward from Xiao and Mian, intending to join Ju and Mo in attacking Shi Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Prince Yue of Zhongshan with fifteen thousand men toward Mengjin, while Huyan Mo, general who guards the east, led the armies of Jing and Si east from Xiao and Mian to join Li Ju and Guo Mo in attacking Shi Sheng.

sentences.zh: 岳克孟津、石樑二戍。

translations.literal: Yue captured the two garrisons at Mengjin and Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue captured the garrisons at Mengjin and Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 斬獲五千餘級，進圍石生於金墉。

translations.literal: He beheaded and captured more than five thousand; then advanced and besieged Shi Sheng at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: He killed and captured more than five thousand men, then advanced to besiege Shi Sheng at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 後趙中山公虎帥步騎四萬，入自成皋關，與岳戰於洛西。

translations.literal: Later Zhao Duke of Zhongshan Hu led forty thousand infantry and cavalry through Chenggao Pass and fought Yue west of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's Duke of Zhongshan, Shi Hu, led forty thousand foot and horse through Chenggao Pass and fought Yue west of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 岳兵敗，中流矢，退保石樑。

translations.literal: Yue's army was defeated; he was struck by a flying arrow and withdrew to hold Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was defeated, wounded by an arrow, and withdrew to Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 虎作塹柵環之，遏絕內外。

translations.literal: Hu built trenches and palisades encircling it, cutting off inside from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu built trenches and palisades around the position, cutting it off completely.

sentences.zh: 岳眾饑甚，殺馬食之。

translations.literal: Yue's troops were extremely hungry and slaughtered horses to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's troops were starving and slaughtered their horses for food.

sentences.zh: 虎又擊呼延謨，斬之。

translations.literal: Hu also attacked Huyan Mo and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu also attacked Huyan Mo and killed him.

sentences.zh: 曜自將兵救岳，虎帥騎三萬逆戰。

translations.literal: Yao personally led troops to rescue Yue; Hu led thirty thousand cavalry to oppose him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao marched in person to relieve Yue; Shi Hu met him with thirty thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 趙前軍將軍劉黑擊虎將石聰於八特阪，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhao Forward General Liu Hei attacked Hu's general Shi Cong at Bate Slope and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao forward general Liu Hei attacked Shi Hu's general Shi Cong at Bate Slope and routed him.

sentences.zh: 曜屯於金谷，夜，軍中無故大驚，士卒奔潰，乃退屯澠池。

translations.literal: Yao encamped at Jingu; at night the army was suddenly thrown into great alarm for no reason, and the soldiers fled in rout; he then withdrew to encamp at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao encamped at Jingu; that night the army panicked without cause and the troops fled in disorder, so he withdrew to Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 夜，又驚潰，遂歸長安。

translations.literal: At night they were alarmed and routed again, and he finally returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: That night they panicked and broke again, and he retreated all the way to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，虎拔石樑，禽岳及其將佐八十餘人，氐、羌三千餘人，皆送襄國，坑其士卒九千人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hu captured Shiliang, seized Yue and more than eighty of his officers, and more than three thousand Di and Qiang; all were sent to Xiangguo, and nine thousand of his soldiers were buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Shi Hu took Shiliang, captured Yue and more than eighty of his officers along with more than three thousand Di and Qiang, sent them to Xiangguo, and buried nine thousand soldiers alive.

sentences.zh: 遂攻王騰於并州，執騰，殺之，坑其士卒七千餘人。

translations.literal: He then attacked Wang Teng in Bingzhou, seized Teng, killed him, and buried more than seven thousand of his soldiers alive.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Wang Teng in Bingzhou, captured and killed him, and buried more than seven thousand of his soldiers alive.

sentences.zh: 曜還長安，素服郊次，哭，七日乃入城，因憤恚成疾。

translations.literal: Yao returned to Chang'an, wore plain mourning garments and waited in the suburbs, wept, and only after seven days entered the city; he then fell ill from grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao returned to Chang'an, waited outside the city in plain mourning dress, wept for seven days before entering, and fell ill from grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 郭默復為石聰所敗，棄妻子南奔建康。

translations.literal: Guo Mo was again defeated by Shi Cong, abandoned his wife and children, and fled south to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo was defeated again by Shi Cong, abandoned his family, and fled south to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 李矩將士陰謀叛降後趙，矩不能討，亦帥眾南歸。

translations.literal: Li Ju's officers and soldiers secretly plotted to rebel and surrender to Later Zhao; Ju could not suppress them, and he also led his troops south in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju's men secretly plotted to defect to Later Zhao; unable to punish them, Ju himself led his forces south in retreat.

sentences.zh: 眾皆道亡，惟郭誦等百餘人隨之；

translations.literal: The masses all fled on the roads; only Guo Song and more than a hundred others followed him;
translations.idiomatic: Most of his followers deserted along the way; only Guo Song and a little over a hundred men stayed with him;

sentences.zh: 卒於魯陽。

translations.literal: He came to his end at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 矩長史崔宣帥其餘眾二千降於後趙。

translations.literal: Ju's chief clerk Cui Xuan led the remaining force of two thousand in surrender to Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan, Ju's chief administrator, surrendered the remaining two thousand troops to Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 於是司、豫、徐、兗之地，率皆入於後趙，以淮為境矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the territories of Si, Yu, Xu, and Yan mostly all entered Later Zhao, with the Huai River as the border.
translations.idiomatic: After this, the regions of Si, Yu, Xu, and Yan largely fell to Later Zhao, which now took the Huai as its frontier.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜以永安王胤為大司馬、大單于，徙封南陽王，置單于台於渭城，其左、右賢王以下，皆以胡、羯、鮮卑、氐、羌豪桀為之。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Liu Yao appointed the Prince of Yong'an, Yin, as Grand Marshal and Grand Chanyu, transferred his enfeoffment to Prince of Nanyang, established the Chanyu Court at Weicheng, and for the Left and Right Worthy Kings and all ranks below, all appointed distinguished men among the Hu, Jie, Xianbei, Di, and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao of Zhao made Prince Yin of Yong'an Grand Marshal and Grand Chanyu, re-enfeoffed him as Prince of Nanyang, set up a Chanyu headquarters at Weicheng, and assigned the Left and Right Worthy Kings and all lower posts to leading figures among the Hu, Jie, Xianbei, Di, and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，以尚書令郗鑒為車騎將軍、都督徐、兗、青三州諸軍事、兗州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinwei, Xi Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Supervisor of military affairs for the three provinces of Xu, Yan, and Qing, and Inspector of Yan, and was stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei day, Xi Jian was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, commander of Xu, Yan, and Qing, inspector of Yan, and posted at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以尚書左僕射荀松為光祿大夫、錄尚書事，尚書鄧攸為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Song was made Grand Master of the Palace and put in charge of Masters of Writing affairs; Master of Writing Deng You was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Xun Song, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with oversight of the secretariat, and Deng You became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍虞胤，元敬皇后之弟也，與左衛將軍南頓王宗俱為帝所親任，典禁兵，直殿內，多聚勇士以為羽翼；

translations.literal: Right Guard General Yu Yin, younger brother of Empress Yuanjing, together with Left Guard General the Prince of Nandun, Zong, were both personally trusted by the emperor; they managed the palace guard, kept watch within the hall, and gathered many warriors as wings of support;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yin, Right Guard General and younger brother of Empress Yuanjing, and Zong, Prince of Nandun and Left Guard General, were both favorites of the emperor; they commanded the palace guard, stood watch within the inner halls, and surrounded themselves with fighting men as a power base;

sentences.zh: 王導、庾亮皆忌之，頗以為言，帝待之愈厚，宮門管鑰，皆以委之。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both resented them and spoke of it on several occasions; the emperor treated them all the more generously, and entrusted them with all the keys to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both distrusted them and said as much, yet the emperor treated them even more warmly and put every palace gate key in their hands.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，亮夜有所表，從宗求鑰；

translations.literal: When the emperor took to his bed with illness, Liang had a memorial to submit at night and sought the keys from Zong;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill in bed, Liang needed to deliver a memorial at night and asked Zong for the keys;

sentences.zh: 宗不與，叱亮使曰：「此汝家門戶邪！」

translations.literal: Zong would not give them and rebuked Liang's messenger, saying: "Is this your family's household gate!"
translations.idiomatic: Zong refused and shouted at Liang's envoy: "Do you think this is your family's front door!"

sentences.zh: 亮益忿之。

translations.literal: Liang grew all the more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's anger only deepened.

sentences.zh: 及帝疾篤，不欲見人，群臣無得進者。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness became grave, he did not wish to see anyone, and none of the officials could gain entry.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's illness turned critical, he refused to receive visitors, and no minister was admitted.

sentences.zh: 亮疑宗、胤及宗兄西陽王羕有異謀，排闥入升御床，見帝流涕，言羕與宗等謀廢大臣，自求輔政，請黜之；

translations.literal: Liang suspected Zong, Yin, and Zong's elder brother the Prince of Xiyang, Yang, of having a divergent plot; he pushed open the door, entered, ascended the imperial couch, wept before the emperor, and said Yang and Zong were plotting to remove the great ministers and sought to assist in government himself, requesting their dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: Liang suspected Zong, Yin, and Zong's elder brother Yang, Prince of Xiyang, of plotting treachery; he burst in, climbed onto the imperial bed, wept before the emperor, and charged that Yang and Zong intended to oust the chief ministers so he could rule in their place, urging their removal;

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝引太宰羕、司徒導、尚書令卞壺、車騎將軍郗鑒、護軍將軍庾亮、領軍將軍陸曄、丹楊尹溫嶠，並受遺詔輔太子，更入殿將兵直宿；

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the emperor summoned Grand Preceptor Yang, Minister of Education Dao, Director of the Masters of Writing Bian Hu, General of Chariots and Cavalry Xi Jian, Protector-General Yu Liang, Commander of the Army Lu Ye, and Governor of Danyang Wen Qiao, all to receive the deathbed edict to assist the heir, and they again entered the hall to command troops on overnight guard;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, the emperor called in Grand Preceptor Yang, Minister of Education Dao, Director Bian Hu, General Xi Jian, Protector-General Yu Liang, Army Commander Lu Ye, and Danyang Governor Wen Qiao to receive the testamentary edict to support the crown prince; they then re-entered the hall to take command of the guard overnight;

sentences.zh: 復拜壺右將軍，亮中書令，曄錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Bian Hu was again appointed Right General, Liang was made Director of the Palace Writers, and Ye was put in charge of Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu was reappointed Right General, Liang was made Director of the Palace Writers, and Ye was given charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，降遺詔。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, the deathbed edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, the testamentary edict was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝崩。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day, the emperor passed away.

sentences.zh: 帝明敏有機斷，故能以弱制強，誅剪逆臣，克復大業。

translations.literal: The emperor was clear-minded and quick in judgment, and therefore was able to use weakness to control strength, execute and eliminate rebellious ministers, and recover the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-eyed and decisive, the emperor had used a weakened throne to master stronger foes, cut down traitors, and restore the dynastic cause.

sentences.zh: 己丑，太子即皇帝位，生五年矣。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the heir ascended the emperor's throne; he was five years of age.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day, the crown prince ascended the throne; he was only five years old.

sentences.zh: 君臣進璽，司徒導以疾不至。

translations.literal: The ministers and ruler presented the imperial seal; Minister of Education Dao, claiming illness, did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: When the court presented the imperial seal, Minister of Education Dao pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 卞壺正色於朝曰：「王公豈社稷之臣邪！

translations.literal: Bian Hu said sternly at court: "How can the Duke be a minister of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu said sternly at court: "Is the Duke truly a servant of the state!

sentences.zh: 大行在殯，嗣皇未立，寧是人臣辭疾之時也！」

translations.literal: The late emperor lies in the coffin, the successor has not yet been established—can this be the time for a subject to plead illness!"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor still lies in state, the new sovereign not yet enthroned—is this really the moment for a minister to stay home sick!"

sentences.zh: 導聞之，輿疾而至。

translations.literal: When Dao heard of it, he came in a carriage despite his illness.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Dao came to court in a sick carriage.

sentences.zh: 大赦，增文武位二等，尊庾後為皇太后。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared; civil and military ranks were raised two grades; Empress Yu was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The court proclaimed a general amnesty, promoted civil and military officials two ranks, and elevated Empress Yu to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 群臣以帝幼沖，奏請太后依漢和熹皇后故事；

translations.literal: The officials, because the emperor was young and tender in years, memorialized requesting the empress dowager to follow the precedent of Empress He and Empress Xi of Han;
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor was still a child, the ministers petitioned that the empress dowager should rule as Empress He and Empress Xi had done under the Han;

sentences.zh: 太后辭讓數四，乃從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager declined several times, and only then assented.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager refused four times before at last consenting.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，癸卯，太后臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day guimao, the empress dowager presided at court and assumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on guimao day, the empress dowager took the throne and ruled in her own name.

sentences.zh: 以司徒導錄尚書事，與中書令庾亮、尚書令卞壺參輔朝政，然事之大要皆決於亮。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Dao was put in charge of Masters of Writing affairs, together with Director of the Palace Writers Yu Liang and Director of the Masters of Writing Bian Hu to assist in governing court affairs, yet the major points of affairs were all decided by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Dao was given charge of the secretariat, alongside Palace Writer Yu Liang and Director Bian Hu to help govern, but every major decision fell to Liang.

sentences.zh: 加郗鑒車騎大將軍，陸曄左光祿大夫，皆開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Xi Jian was given the additional title of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Lu Ye was made Left Grand Master of the Palace, and both were granted the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies with their own offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Lu Ye to Left Grand Master of the Palace, and both received offices with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 以南頓王宗為驃騎將軍，虞胤為大宗正。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nandun, Zong, was made General of Agile Cavalry, and Yu Yin was made Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, Prince of Nandun, was made General of Agile Cavalry, and Yu Yin was appointed Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 尚書召樂廣子謨為郡中正，庾鈱族人怡為廷尉評，謨、怡各稱父命不就。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing summoned Yue Guang's son Mo to be district chief rectifier and a kinsman of Yu Qian, Yi, to be reviewer for the Minister of Justice; Mo and Yi each claimed their fathers' orders and would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing summoned Yue Mo, son of Yue Guang, as district chief rectifier and Yi, a clansman of Yu Qian, as judicial reviewer; both cited their fathers' wishes and declined.

sentences.zh: 卞壺奏曰：「人無非父而生，職無非事而立，有父必有命，居職必有悔。

translations.literal: Bian Hu memorialized, saying: "No man is born without a father, no office is established without business; where there is a father there must be orders, and where one holds office there must be responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu submitted a memorial: "No one is born without a father, and no post exists without duties to fulfill; fathers give orders, and office carries obligations.

sentences.zh: 有家各私其子，則為王者無民，君臣之道廢矣。

translations.literal: If every family privately favors its own sons, then the king would have no people, and the way of ruler and subject would be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: If every household could favor its own sons, the ruler would have no subjects and the bond between lord and minister would collapse.

sentences.zh: 樂廣、庾鈱受寵聖世，身非己有，況及後嗣而可專哉！

translations.literal: Yue Guang and Yu Qian received favor in this sage age; their persons are not their own possessions—how much less can they monopolize their offspring!
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang and Yu Qian owed their positions to imperial favor—their very persons were not their own; how much less could they dispose of their sons as they pleased!

sentences.zh: 所居之職，若順夫群心，則戰戍者之父母皆當命子以不處也。」

translations.literal: The office they occupy—if one followed every man's heart, then the parents of every soldier on campaign ought to order their sons not to take up their posts."
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, every parent of a soldier on campaign could order a son not to serve."

sentences.zh: 謨、怡不得已，各就職。

translations.literal: Mo and Yi, having no alternative, each took up their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Reluctantly, Mo and Yi each accepted their posts.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，葬明帝於武平陵。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Emperor Ming was buried at Wuping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day, Emperor Ming was interred at Wuping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，癸巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the new moon of guisi day, there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆與段氏方睦，為段牙謀，使之徙都；

translations.literal: Murong Hui was on friendly terms with the Duan clan and schemed on behalf of Duan Ya, causing him to move his capital;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui was then on good terms with the Duan clan and persuaded Duan Ya to relocate his capital;

sentences.zh: 牙從之，即去令支，國人不樂。

translations.literal: Ya assented, immediately left Lingzhi, and the people of the state were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Ya agreed, abandoned Lingzhi at once, and his subjects were unhappy with the move.

sentences.zh: 段疾陸眷之孫遼欲奪其位，以徙都為牙罪，十二月，帥國人攻牙，殺之，自立。

translations.literal: Duan Liaow, grandson of Duan Jilujuan, wished to seize his position; taking the move of the capital as Ya's crime, in the twelfth month he led the people of the state to attack Ya, killed him, and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liaow, grandson of Duan Jilujuan, sought to take his place; citing the capital move as Ya's offense, in the twelfth month he rallied the nation against Ya, killed him, and proclaimed himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 段氏自務勿塵以來，日益強盛，其地西接漁陽，東界遼水，所統胡、晉三萬餘戶，控弦四五萬騎。

translations.literal: Since Wuwuchen of the Duan clan, they had grown daily in strength; their territory bordered Yuyang in the west and the Liao River in the east; the Hu and Jin households under their rule numbered more than thirty thousand, and their bowmen totaled forty to fifty thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: From Wuwuchen's day the Duan had grown steadily stronger; their lands stretched from Yuyang in the west to the Liao River in the east, they ruled more than thirty thousand Hu and Han households, and could field forty to fifty thousand mounted archers.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史陶侃以寧州刺史王堅不能禦寇，是歲，表零陵太守南陽尹奉為寧州刺史以代之。

translations.literal: Tao Kan, Inspector of Jing Province, because Wang Jian, Inspector of Ning Province, could not repel the invaders, that year memorialized recommending Yin Feng of Nanyang, Administrator of Lingling, as Inspector of Ning Province to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, governor of Jing, finding Ning inspector Wang Jian unable to hold off the invaders, that year recommended Yin Feng of Nanyang, administrator of Lingling, to replace him as inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 先是，王遜在寧州，蠻酋梁水太守爨量、益州太守李逖，皆叛附於成。

translations.literal: Previously, when Wang Xun was in Ning Province, the tribal chieftain and Administrator of Liangshui, Cuan Liang, and Administrator of Yizhou, Li Ti, both rebelled and submitted to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Wang Xun governed Ning, the tribal leader Cuan Liang, administrator of Liangshui, and Li Ti, administrator of Yizhou, had both rebelled and joined Cheng.

sentences.zh: 遜討之不能克。

translations.literal: Xun campaigned against them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fought them but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 奉至州，重募徼外夷刺爨量，殺之，諭降李逖，州境遂安。

translations.literal: When Feng arrived at the province, he heavily recruited foreign Yi from beyond the frontier to assassinate Cuan Liang and killed him; he persuaded Li Ti to surrender, and the borders of the province were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng took office, he hired frontier tribesmen to ambush and kill Cuan Liang, persuaded Li Ti to submit, and the province was soon quiet again.

sentences.zh: 代王賀辱卒，弟紇那立。

translations.literal: He Ruchou, king of Dai, died; his younger brother Henade was established.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruchou, king of Dai, died, and his younger brother Henade succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗明皇帝下鹹和元年（

translations.literal: Below Emperor Ming of the Succeeding Ancestor—the first year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Ming, Xianhe, year 1 (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元三二六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, corresponding to the year 326 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, corresponding to 326 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, a general amnesty was declared and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 趙以汝南五鹹為太尉、錄尚書事，光祿太夫劉綏為大司徒，卜泰為大司空。

translations.literal: Zhao appointed Wang Xian of Runan as Grand Commandant and put him in charge of Masters of Writing affairs; Liu Sui, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, was made Grand Minister of Education; Bu Tai was made Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao made Runan Prince Wang Xian Grand Commandant with charge of the secretariat, Liu Sui Grand Minister of Education, and Bu Tai Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 劉後疾病，趙主曜問所欲言，劉氏泣曰：「妾幼鞠於叔父昶，願陛下貴之。

translations.literal: Empress Liu fell ill; Zhao's ruler Liu Yao asked what she wished to say; Lady Liu wept and said: "I was reared in childhood by my uncle Chang; I wish Your Majesty to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu fell ill; when Liu Yao asked her final wishes, she wept and said: "My uncle Chang raised me from childhood; I beg Your Majesty to elevate him.

sentences.zh: 叔父皚之女芳有德色，願以備後宮。」

translations.literal: My uncle Gao's daughter Fang has virtue and beauty; I wish her to be placed in the rear palace."
translations.idiomatic: My uncle Gao's daughter Fang is virtuous and beautiful; I ask that she join the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 言終而卒。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died as soon as she had spoken.

sentences.zh: 曜以昶為侍中、大司徒、錄尚書事，立芳為皇后；

translations.literal: Yao made Chang Palace Attendant, Grand Minister of Education, and put him in charge of Masters of Writing affairs, and established Fang as empress;
translations.idiomatic: Yao made Chang a palace attendant and Grand Minister of Education with charge of the secretariat, and made Fang empress;

sentences.zh: 尋又以昶為太保。

translations.literal: Soon after he again made Chang Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also appointed Chang Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 三月，後趙主勒夜微行檢察諸營衛，繼金帛以賂門者，求出。

translations.literal: In the third month, Later Zhao's ruler Shi Le by night went out incognito to inspect the various camps and guards; he brought gold and silk to bribe the gatekeepers, seeking release.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Later Zhao ruler Shi Le went out at night in disguise to inspect the camps and guards; he then offered gold and silk to the gatekeepers, trying to get out.

sentences.zh: 永昌門候王假欲收捕之，從者至，乃止。

translations.literal: Wang Jia, gate officer of Yongchang Gate, wished to seize and capture him; when his attendants arrived, he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, guard of Yongchang Gate, moved to arrest him, but stopped when Le's attendants arrived.

sentences.zh: 旦，召假，以為振忠都尉，爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned Jia and made him Commandant of Loyal Inspiration, enfeoffing him as Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he summoned Jia, made him Commandant of Inspiring Loyalty, and enfeoffed him as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 勒召記室參軍徐光，光醉不至，黜為牙門。

translations.literal: Le summoned his secretariat adjutant Xu Guang; Guang, being drunk, did not come, and was demoted to gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: Le summoned his recorder Xu Guang, but Guang came drunk and was demoted to gate duty.

sentences.zh: 光侍直，有慍色，勒怒，並其妻子囚之。

translations.literal: Guang attended on duty with an angry expression; Le was enraged and imprisoned him together with his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang reported for duty looking sullen, Le flew into a rage and imprisoned him along with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，後趙將石生寇汝南，執內史祖濟。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Sheng raided Runan and seized Interior Minister Zu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Sheng attacked Runan and captured interior minister Zu Ji.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，泉陵公劉遐卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guihai, Duke Liu Xia of Quanling died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai day, Duke Liu Xia of Quanling died.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以車騎大將軍郗鑒領徐州刺史；

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Xi Jian was made acting Inspector of Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day, Grand General Xi Jian was appointed acting inspector of Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍郭默為北中郎將、監淮北諸軍事，領遐部曲。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Barbarians Guo Mo was made North Central Commandant, overseer of military affairs north of the Huai, commanding Xia's former troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was made North Central Commandant to oversee the Huai-north command and take over Xia's forces.

sentences.zh: 遐子肇尚幼，遐妹夫田防及故將史迭等不樂他屬，共以肇襲遐故位而叛。

translations.literal: Xia's son Zhao was still young; Xia's brother-in-law Tian Fang and former generals Shi Die and others, displeased at serving another master, together had Zhao succeed to Xia's former position and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's son Zhao was still a child; Tian Fang, Xia's brother-in-law, and former officers including Shi Die, unwilling to serve a new commander, installed Zhao in his father's post and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 臨淮太守劉矯掩襲遐營，斬防等。

translations.literal: Liu Jiao, Administrator of Linhuai, launched a surprise attack on Xia's camp and beheaded Fang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiao, administrator of Linhuai, struck Xia's camp by surprise and killed Fang and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 遐妻，邵續女也，驍果有父風。

translations.literal: Xia's wife was the daughter of Shao Xu; she was bold and resolute and had her father's mettle.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's wife was Shao Xu's daughter—fierce and resolute, with her father's fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 遐嘗為後趙所圍，妻單將數騎，拔遐出於萬眾之中。

translations.literal: Xia had once been besieged by Later Zhao; his wife alone led several horsemen and extricated Xia from among tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhao once besieged Xia, his wife rode out alone with a handful of men and pulled him from the midst of ten thousand foes.

sentences.zh: 及田防等欲作亂，遐妻止之，不從，乃密起火，燒甲仗都盡，故防等卒敗。

translations.literal: When Tian Fang and others wished to raise a revolt, Xia's wife stopped them; they would not listen, so she secretly set a fire that burned all the armor and weapons, and therefore Fang and the others were finally defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Fang and his allies plotted rebellion, Xia's wife tried to stop them; when they refused, she secretly set a fire that destroyed all their arms and armor, and Fang's plot collapsed.

sentences.zh: 詔以肇襲遐爵。

translations.literal: An edict had Zhao succeed to Xia's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhao to inherit Xia's title.

sentences.zh: 司徒導稱疾不朝，而私送郗鑒。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Dao claimed illness and did not attend court, yet privately saw Xi Jian off.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Dao stayed away from court claiming illness, yet went privately to bid Xi Jian farewell.

sentences.zh: 卞壺奏「導虧法從私，無大臣之節，請免官。」

translations.literal: Bian Hu memorialized: "Dao has violated the law in favor of private interest and lacks the integrity of a great minister; I request his dismissal from office."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu memorialized that "Dao has broken the law for private reasons and shown none of a great minister's dignity; he should be removed from office."

sentences.zh: 雖事寢不行，舉朝憚之。

translations.literal: Although the matter was shelved and not carried out, the whole court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal went nowhere, the entire court stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 壺儉素廉絜，裁斷切直，當官干實，性不弘裕，不肯苟同時好，故為諸名士所少。

translations.literal: Hu was frugal, plain, and honest and pure; his judgments were sharp and direct; in office he was practical and solid; by nature he was not broad and generous and would not casually agree with the tastes of the age—therefore he was somewhat disliked by the various celebrated gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu lived plainly and judged sharply; he was practical in office, uncompromising by nature, and unwilling to pander to fashion—so the leading gentlemen looked on him with little favor.

sentences.zh: 阮孚謂之曰：「卿常無閒泰，如含瓦石，不亦勞乎！」

translations.literal: Ruan Fu said to him: "You are always without leisure and ease, as if holding tile and stone in your mouth—is it not exhausting!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu told him: "You never seem at ease, as though you were chewing gravel—isn't that exhausting!"

sentences.zh: 壺曰：「諸君子以道德恢弘，風流相尚，執鄙吝者，非壺而誰！」

translations.literal: Hu said: "You gentlemen enlarge yourselves with moral virtue and esteem one another for elegance and flair—if anyone is grasping and mean, who if not Hu!"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hu replied: "You gentlemen enlarge virtue and compete in refinement—if anyone is petty and stingy, who else but me!"

sentences.zh: 時貴遊子弟多慕王澄、謝鯤為放達，壺厲色於朝曰：「悖禮傷教，罪莫大焉；

translations.literal: At that time the sons of the nobility mostly admired Wang Cheng and Xie Kun for their free and unrestrained ways; Hu said sternly at court: "To violate ritual and harm teaching—there is no greater crime;
translations.idiomatic: Many young nobles then admired Wang Cheng and Xie Kun for their libertine ways; Bian Hu said sternly at court: "Defying propriety and corrupting morals is the greatest of crimes;

sentences.zh: 中朝傾覆，實由於此。」

translations.literal: The collapse of the central court in fact arose from this."
translations.idiomatic: The fall of the central court came from just such conduct."

sentences.zh: 欲奏推之，王導、庾亮不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: He wished to memorialize recommending their prosecution; Wang Dao and Yu Liang would not listen, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to impeach them, but Wang Dao and Yu Liang refused to act, and he let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 成人討越巂斯叟，破之。

translations.literal: Cheng sent troops against the Sisou of Yuexi and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng attacked the Sisou tribe in Yuexi and broke them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，觀陽烈侯應詹卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guichou, Marquis Ying Zhan of Guanyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou day, Marquis Ying Zhan of Guanyang died.

sentences.zh: 初，王導輔政，以寬和得眾。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wang Dao assisted in government, he won the masses through leniency and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: At first, under Wang Dao's regency, his lenient and conciliatory manner won broad support.

sentences.zh: 及庾亮用事，任法裁物，頗失人心。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang came to power, he relied on law to judge affairs and lost considerable popular support.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Liang took control, his strict reliance on law alienated many.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史祖約，自以輩不後郗、卞，而不豫顧命，又望開府復不得，及諸表請多不見許，遂懷怨望。

translations.literal: Zu Yue, Inspector of Yu Province, considered that in seniority he was not behind Xi and Bian, yet was not included in the deathbed appointment; he also hoped for an independent office but again did not obtain it; moreover many of his various petitions were not approved—thereupon he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue, governor of Yu, felt his standing matched Xi Jian's and Bian Hu's, yet he was left out of the deathbed regents; he also sought an independent headquarters in vain, and many of his petitions went unanswered—so bitterness took root.

sentences.zh: 及遺詔褒進大臣，又不及約與陶侃，二人皆疑庾亮刪之。

translations.literal: When the deathbed edict praised and promoted the great ministers, it again did not include Yue and Tao Kan; both men suspected Yu Liang had deleted their names.
translations.idiomatic: When the testament omitted praise for Yue and Tao Kan along with the other ministers, both suspected Yu Liang had struck their names from the edict.

sentences.zh: 歷陽內史蘇峻，有功於國，威望漸著，有銳卒萬人，器械甚精，朝廷以江外寄之；

translations.literal: Su Jun, Interior Minister of Liyang, had merit for the state; his prestige gradually grew prominent; he had ten thousand sharp troops and extremely fine weapons; the court entrusted the regions beyond the Yangzi to him;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun of Liyang had served the dynasty well; his reputation and power grew, he commanded ten thousand elite troops with excellent arms, and the court relied on him to hold the lower Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 而峻頗懷驕溢，有輕朝廷之志，招納亡命，眾力日多，皆仰食縣官，運漕相屬，稍不如意，輒肆忿言。

translations.literal: yet Jun harbored considerable arrogance and excess, had a mind to look down on the court, recruited fugitives, his forces daily increased, all fed by official county supplies, transport of grain tribute continuous—at the slightest dissatisfaction he would vent angry words.
translations.idiomatic: yet Jun grew arrogant, began to scorn the court, took in fugitives, and swelled his ranks—all on the public payroll, with supply convoys unending—and grumbled loudly whenever anything displeased him.

sentences.zh: 亮既疑峻、約，又畏侃之得眾，八月，以丹楊尹溫嶠為都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，鎮武昌；

translations.literal: Liang both suspected Jun and Yue and also feared Kan's hold on the masses; in the eighth month he made Wen Qiao, Governor of Danyang, Supervisor of military affairs for Jiang Province and Inspector of Jiang Province, stationed at Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: Liang distrusted both Jun and Yue and feared Tao Kan's popularity; in the eighth month he posted Wen Qiao as commander of Jiangzhou from Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射王舒為會稽內史，以廣聲援；

translations.literal: Wang Shu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Interior Minister of Kuaiji to broaden strategic support;
translations.idiomatic: and made Wang Shu, vice director of the Masters of Writing, interior minister of Kuaiji to extend support nearer the capital;

sentences.zh: 又修石頭以備之。

translations.literal: He also repaired Shitou as a precaution against them.
translations.idiomatic: He also fortified Shitou as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 丹楊尹阮孚以太后臨朝，政出舅族，謂所親曰：「今江東創業尚淺，主幼時艱，庾亮年少，德信未孚，以吾觀之，亂將作矣。」

translations.literal: Ruan Fu, Governor of Danyang, because the empress dowager presided at court and government issued from the maternal kin clan, said to those close to him: "Now the founding of Jiangdong is still shallow, the ruler is young and the times are hard, Yu Liang is young and his virtue and trust have not yet won acceptance—in my view, disorder is about to arise."
translations.idiomatic: Danyang governor Ruan Fu, seeing the empress dowager in power and the government in the hands of her clan, told his confidants: "The eastern realm is still young, the emperor a child in troubled times, and Yu Liang too young to command trust—in my view, rebellion is coming."

sentences.zh: 遂求出為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to be sent out as Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to be posted away as governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 孚，鹹之子也。

translations.literal: Fu was the son of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu was the son of Ruan Xian.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，立帝母弟岳為吳王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Yue, was established as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the emperor's own younger brother Yue was made Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 南頓王宗自以失職怨望，又素與蘇峻善，庾亮欲誅之，宗亦欲廢執政。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nandun, Zong, resentful at having lost his position, and having long been on good terms with Su Jun, Yu Liang wished to execute him; Zong also wished to depose those holding power.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, Prince of Nandun, bitter over his loss of office and long friendly with Su Jun, was marked for death by Yu Liang; Zong in turn plotted to oust the regents.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞鐘雅劾宗謀反，亮使右衛將軍趙胤收之。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhong Ya impeached Zong for plotting rebellion; Liang sent Right Guard General Zhao Yin to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhong Ya charged Zong with treason, and Liang dispatched Right Guard General Zhao Yin to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 宗以兵拒戰，為胤所殺，貶其族為馬氏，三子綽、超、演皆廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Zong resisted with troops in battle, was killed by Yin, his clan was degraded to the surname Ma, and his three sons Chuo, Chao, and Yan were all demoted to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Zong took up arms and was slain by Zhao Yin; his house was stripped of its imperial surname and renamed Ma, and his three sons Chuo, Chao, and Yan were reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 免太宰西陽王羕，降封弋陽縣王，大宗正虞胤左遷桂陽太守。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xiyang Yang, was removed from office, demoted to Prince of Yiyang County, and Yu Yin, Director of the Imperial Clan, was transferred to the left as Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Prince of Xiyang and Grand Preceptor, was dismissed and demoted to Prince of Yiyang County; Yu Yin, chief of the imperial clan, was relegated to governor of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 宗，宗室近屬；

translations.literal: Zong was a close kinsman of the imperial house;
translations.idiomatic: Zong was a near relative of the throne;

sentences.zh: 羕，先帝保傅。

translations.literal: Yang was the late emperor's tutor and companion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had been tutor and guardian to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 亮一旦剪黜，由是失遠近之心。

translations.literal: Liang in one stroke cut and demoted them, and thereby lost the hearts of those near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's sudden purge cost him the loyalty of court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 宗黨卞闡亡奔蘇峻，亮符峻送闡，峻保匿不與。

translations.literal: Zong's partisan Bian Chan fled to Su Jun; Liang issued a warrant to Jun to send Chan back, but Jun sheltered and concealed him and would not surrender him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's follower Bian Chan fled to Su Jun; Liang ordered Jun to hand him over, but Jun hid him and refused.

sentences.zh: 宗之死也，帝不之知，久之，帝問亮曰：「常日白頭公何在？」

translations.literal: When Zong died, the emperor did not know of it; after a long time, the emperor asked Liang, saying: "Where is the white-haired lord of ordinary days?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew nothing of Zong's death; long afterward he asked Liang, "Where is the old white-haired gentleman I used to see?"

sentences.zh: 亮對以謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: Liang answered that he had been executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied that Zong had been put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「舅言人作賊，便殺之；

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "Uncle, when you say someone is a bandit, you have him killed;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "Uncle, when you call a man a thief, you kill him;

sentences.zh: 人言舅作賊，當如何！」

translations.literal: When people say Uncle is a bandit, what is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: but if people call you the thief—what then!"

sentences.zh: 亮懼，變色。

translations.literal: Liang feared and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Liang turned pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 趙將黃秀等寇酇，順陽太守魏該帥眾奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Zhao general Huang Xiu and others raided Zan; Wei Gai, Administrator of Shunyang, led his forces in flight to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao generals including Huang Xiu raided Zan; Wei Gai, governor of Shunyang, fled with his troops to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒用程遐之謀，營鄴宮，使世子弘鎮鄴，配禁兵萬人，車騎所統五十四營悉配之，以驍騎將軍領門臣祭酒王陽專統六夷以輔之。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le adopted Cheng Xia's plan, built the palace at Ye, had the heir apparent Hong guard Ye, assigned ten thousand palace troops, and all fifty-four camps under the Chariots and Cavalry were allotted to him; the Flying Cavalry General and Libationer of the Gate Retainers Wang Yang was put in sole command of the Six Barbarian peoples to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao's King Le followed Cheng Xia's advice: he built a palace at Ye, posted the heir Hong there with ten thousand elite guards and all fifty-four camps formerly under the Chariots and Cavalry, and set Wang Yang, Flying Cavalry General and chief of the gate corps, to lead the Six Barbarian contingents in support.

sentences.zh: 中山公虎自以功多，無去鄴之意，及修三台，遷其家室，虎由是怨程遐。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Hu, judging his own merit great, had no intention of leaving Ye; when the Three Terraces were repaired and his household moved, Hu henceforth resented Cheng Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hu of Zhongshan, proud of his achievements, refused to leave Ye; when the Three Terraces were rebuilt and his family was relocated, he came to hate Cheng Xia.

sentences.zh: 十一月，後趙石聰攻壽春，祖約屢表請救，朝廷不為出兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Later Zhao's Shi Cong attacked Shouchun; Zu Yue repeatedly submitted memorials asking for rescue, but the court would not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Shi Cong of Later Zhao besieged Shouchun; Zu Yue pleaded repeatedly for relief, but the court sent no army.

sentences.zh: 聰遂進寇逡遒、阜陵，殺掠五千餘人。

translations.literal: Cong then advanced to raid Xunqu and Fuling, killing and plundering more than five thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Cong pushed on to ravage Xunqu and Fuling, killing and looting more than five thousand people.

sentences.zh: 建康大震，詔加司徒導大司馬、假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事以御之，軍於江寧。

translations.literal: Jiankang was greatly shaken; an edict added to Grand Tutor Dao the title Grand Marshal, loaned the yellow battle-axe, and made him Supervisor of all armies within and without to oppose them; he encamped at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Panic seized Jiankang; Dao was made Grand Marshal with the yellow axe and supreme command, and camped at Jiangning to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻遣其將韓晃擊石聰，走之，導解大司馬。

translations.literal: Su Jun sent his general Han Huang to strike Shi Cong and drive him off; Dao was relieved of the Grand Marshalship.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun dispatched Han Huang, who routed Shi Cong; Dao then relinquished the grand marshal's seal.

sentences.zh: 朝議又欲作塗塘以遏胡寇，祖約曰：「是棄我也！」

translations.literal: Court deliberation again wished to build a barrier dike to check the barbarian raiders; Zu Yue said: "This is abandoning me!"
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated building an earthen barrier against the northern raids; Zu Yue cried, "You mean to cast me off!"

sentences.zh: 益懷憤恚。

translations.literal: He grew all the more in resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: His anger hardened.

sentences.zh: 十二月，濟岷太守劉闓等殺下邳內史夏侯嘉，以下邳叛，降於後趙。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liu Kan, Administrator of Jimin, and others killed Xia Houjia, Interior Minister of Xiapi, rebelled with Xiapi, and surrendered to Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liu Kan, governor of Jimin, and others killed Xia Houjia, interior minister of Xiapi, rebelled with the city, and submitted to Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 石瞻攻河南太守王瞻於邾，拔之。

translations.literal: Shi Zhan attacked Wang Zhan, Administrator of Henan, at Zhu and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhan stormed Zhu, where Wang Zhan governed Henan, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 彭城內史劉續復據蘭陵石城，石瞻攻拔之。

translations.literal: Liu Xu, Interior Minister of Pengcheng, again held Lanling's Shicheng; Shi Zhan attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu of Pengcheng reoccupied Shicheng in Lanling; Shi Zhan took it by assault.

sentences.zh: 後趙王勒以牙門將王波為記室參軍，典定九流，始立秀、孝試經之制。

translations.literal: Later Zhao King Le made Wang Bo, a Ya Men general, a Recording Army adjutant, to preside over classification of the Nine Currents, and for the first time established the system of testing classics for the Xiucai and Xiaolian degrees.
translations.idiomatic: King Le of Later Zhao appointed gate officer Wang Bo recorder and adjutant to classify candidates and institute examinations in the classics for Xiucai and Xiaolian recruits.

sentences.zh: 張竣畏趙人之逼，是歲，徙隴西、南安民二千餘家於姑臧，又遣修好於成，以書勸成主雄去尊號，稱籓於晉。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, fearing the Zhao people's pressure, in this year moved more than two thousand households from Longxi and Nan'an to Guzang, and also sent envoys to establish good relations with Cheng, writing to urge Lord of Cheng Xiong to discard his exalted title and declare himself a vassal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of Zhao pressure, Zhang Jun that year relocated over two thousand families from Longxi and Nan'an to Guzang and opened talks with Cheng, urging Li Xiong to drop his imperial style and acknowledge Jin as overlord.

sentences.zh: 雄復書曰：「吾過為士大夫所推，然本無心於帝王，思為晉室元功之臣，掃除氛埃；

translations.literal: Xiong replied in a letter, saying: "I was excessively pushed forward by the gentry and officials, yet originally I had no heart for emperorship; I wished to be a founding minister of the Jin house and sweep away the murky air;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong answered: "The gentry pressed this crown on me, but I never coveted the throne; I meant to serve Jin as a founding pillar and clear the land of chaos;

sentences.zh: 而晉室陵遲，德聲不振，引領東望，有年月矣。

translations.literal: yet the Jin house declined, its virtuous renown did not resound, neck outstretched looking east—I have done so for months and years.
translations.idiomatic: yet Jin itself has waned and its authority faded; I have yearned eastward toward the capital for years.

sentences.zh: 會獲來貺，情在暗至，有何已已。」

translations.literal: When I received your envoys and gifts, my feeling was of long-awaited arrival from afar—how could it ever cease?"
translations.idiomatic: Your envoy's arrival felt like answered longing from afar—I welcome it without reserve."

sentences.zh: 自是聘使相繼。

translations.literal: From this envoys and messengers followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys thereafter shuttled between the two realms.

sentences.zh: 肅宗明皇帝下鹹和二年（

translations.literal: Under the chronicle of the Illustrious Ancestor, Emperor Ming—the second year of Xianhe (
translations.idiomatic: Under the chronicle of Emperor Ming, the Illustrious Ancestor—the second year of Xianhe (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元三二七年）

translations.literal: Dinghai, corresponding to the year 327 CE)
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai, corresponding to 327 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朱提太守楊術與成將羅恆戰於台登，兵敗，術死。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yang Shu, Administrator of Zhuti, fought with Cheng general Luo Heng at Taideng, was defeated in battle, and Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yang Shu of Zhuti fought Luo Heng of Cheng at Taideng, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，甲申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day Jiashen—the first of the month—the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the new moon of Jiashen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 趙武衛將軍劉朗帥騎三萬襲楊難敵於仇池，弗克，掠三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Zhao Military Guard General Liu Lang led thirty thousand cavalry to raid Yang Nanqi at Chouchi, did not overcome him, plundered more than three thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lang, Military Guard general of Zhao, led thirty thousand horse against Yang Nanqi at Chouchi, failed to take him, carried off more than three thousand households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 張竣聞趙兵為後趙所敗，乃去趙官爵，復稱晉大將軍、涼州牧，遣武威太守竇濤、金城太守張閬、武興太守辛巖、揚烈將軍宋輯等帥眾數萬，東會韓璞，攻掠趙秦州諸郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun heard that Zhao troops had been defeated by Later Zhao; thereupon he cast off Zhao titles and ranks, again styled himself Jin's Grand General and Governor of Liang Province, and sent Dou Tao, Administrator of Wuwei, Zhang Lang, Administrator of Jincheng, Xin Yan, Administrator of Wuxing, Yanglie General Song Ji, and others to lead forces numbering in the tens of thousands east to join Han Pu and raid and plunder the commanderies of Zhao's Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhao's armies had been beaten by Later Zhao, Zhang Jun renounced Zhao honors, resumed the titles Grand General and Governor of Liangzhou under Jin, and sent Dou Tao of Wuwei, Zhang Lang of Jincheng, Xin Yan of Wuxing, Yanglie General Song Ji, and others east with tens of thousands of men to join Han Pu in raiding Qinzhou under Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙南陽王胤將兵擊之，屯狄道。

translations.literal: Zhao's Prince of Nanyang Yin led troops to strike them and encamped at Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, Prince of Nanyang under Zhao, marched against them and camped at Didao.

sentences.zh: 枹罕護軍辛晏告急。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Fuhan Xin Yan reported urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yan, Protector-General of Fuhan, sent an urgent plea for help.

sentences.zh: 秋，駿使韓璞、辛巖救之。

translations.literal: In autumn, Jun sent Han Pu and Xin Yan to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Jun dispatched Han Pu and Xin Yan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 璞進度沃干嶺。

translations.literal: Pu advanced crossing the Wogan Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Pu crossed the Wogan Ridge and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 巖欲速戰，璞曰：「夏末以來，日星數有變，不可輕動。

translations.literal: Yan wished for a quick battle; Pu said: "Since the end of summer, sun and stars have repeatedly shown portents—it cannot be lightly acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yan urged an immediate fight; Pu said, "Since late summer sun and stars have shown bad omens—we must not move rashly.

sentences.zh: 且曜與石勒相攻，胤必不能久與我相守也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Liu Yao and Shi Le are attacking each other; Yin certainly cannot long stand against us in stalemate."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, with Liu Yao and Shi Le at each other's throats, Yin cannot keep this standoff long."

sentences.zh: 與胤夾洮相持七十餘日。

translations.literal: They faced Yin across the Tao River in stalemate for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: They faced Yin across the Tao for over seventy days.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，璞遣辛巖督運於金城，胤聞之，曰：「韓璞之眾，十倍於吾。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Pu sent Xin Yan to supervise transport at Jincheng; Yin heard of it and said: "Han Pu's masses are ten times ours.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Pu sent Xin Yan to oversee supplies at Jincheng; Yin heard and said, "Han Pu outnumbers us ten to one.

sentences.zh: 吾糧不多，難以持久。

translations.literal: Our grain is not abundant—we cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Our stores are thin and we cannot hold out.

sentences.zh: 今虜分兵運糧，天授我也。

translations.literal: Now the enemy has divided forces to transport grain—Heaven has granted this to me.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have split their army to haul grain—Heaven has handed me the chance.

sentences.zh: 若敗辛巖，璞等自潰」。

translations.literal: If we defeat Xin Yan, Pu and the rest will collapse of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Crush Xin Yan, and Pu's host will fall apart by itself."

sentences.zh: 乃帥騎三千襲巖於沃干嶺，敗之，遂前逼璞營，璞眾大潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led three thousand cavalry to raid Yan at Wogan Ridge, defeated him, then advanced to press Pu's camp, and Pu's forces collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: He led three thousand cavalry against Yan at Wogan Ridge, routed him, then drove on Pu's camp until Pu's army broke completely.

sentences.zh: 胤乘勝追奔，濟河，攻拔令居，斬首二萬級，進據振武，河西大駭。

translations.literal: Yin, riding victory in pursuit, crossed the river, attacked and took Lingju, beheaded twenty thousand, advanced to hold Zhenwu, and the lands west of the river were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pursued the rout, crossed the river, took Lingju, took twenty thousand heads, seized Zhenwu, and terror spread across Hexi.

sentences.zh: 張閬、辛晏帥其眾數萬降趙，駿遂失河南之地。

translations.literal: Zhang Lang and Xin Yan led their masses, numbering in the tens of thousands, in surrender to Zhao; Jun thereupon lost the lands south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang and Xin Yan surrendered with tens of thousands of men; Jun lost all of Henan west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 庾亮以蘇峻在歷陽，終為禍亂，欲下詔征之，訪於司徒導。

translations.literal: Yu Liang, because Su Jun was at Liyang and would ultimately become disaster and disorder, wished to issue an edict summoning him and consulted Grand Tutor Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang feared Su Jun at Liyang would yet bring calamity and planned to summon him by imperial edict; he sought Wang Dao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 導曰：「峻猜險，必不奉詔，不若且苞容之。」

translations.literal: Dao said: "Jun is suspicious and dangerous—he will certainly not obey the edict; better for now to bear with and contain him."
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "Jun is treacherous and will refuse the summons—you would do better to tolerate him for now."

sentences.zh: 亮言於朝曰：「峻狼子野心，終必為亂。

translations.literal: Liang spoke in court, saying: "Jun has the heart of a wolf cub—he will ultimately rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Liang told the court, "Jun has the heart of a wolf cub and will rebel in the end.

sentences.zh: 今日征之，縱不順命，為禍猶淺；

translations.literal: If we summon him today, even should he not obey, the harm would still be shallow;
translations.idiomatic: If we act now, even disobedience would do less harm than waiting;

sentences.zh: 若復經年，不可複製，猶七國之於漢也。」

translations.literal: if another year passes, we cannot again grasp control—it will be like the Seven Kingdoms against Han."
translations.idiomatic: delay another year and he will be unmanageable, like the seven princes against Han Wudi."

sentences.zh: 朝臣無敢難者，獨光祿大夫卞壺爭之曰：「峻擁強兵，逼近京邑，路不終朝。

translations.literal: No court official dared to oppose; only Household Counsellor Bian Hu disputed it, saying: "Jun holds strong troops and presses close to the capital—a march of less than one morning.
translations.idiomatic: No one gainsaid him except Bian Hu, Household Counsellor, who protested: "Jun commands a strong army within a morning's march of the capital.

sentences.zh: 一旦有變，易為蹉跌，宜深思之！」

translations.literal: Once there is a change, it is easy to stumble and fall—you should think deeply on this!"
translations.idiomatic: At the first crisis we may stumble beyond recovery—think hard before you move!"

sentences.zh: 亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 壺知必敗，與溫嶠書曰：「元規召峻意定，此國之大事。

translations.literal: Hu knew defeat was certain and wrote to Wen Qiao, saying: "Yuankui's intent to summon Jun is fixed—this is a great matter for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hu saw disaster coming and wrote Wen Qiao: "Yuankui is set on summoning Jun—a matter of national life or death.

sentences.zh: 峻已出狂意，而召之，是更速其禍也，必縱毒蜇以向朝廷。

translations.literal: Jun has already revealed mad intent, yet to summon him is only to hasten his disaster; he will surely unleash poison stings against the court.
translations.idiomatic: Jun already shows reckless defiance; calling him in will only hasten catastrophe and turn his venom on the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷威雖盛，不知果可擒不；

translations.literal: Though the court's might is great, one does not know whether he can indeed be captured or not;
translations.idiomatic: The court looks strong, but whether Jun can really be taken is far from certain;

sentences.zh: 王公亦同此情。

translations.literal: Duke Wang shares this feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wang feels the same.

sentences.zh: 吾與之爭甚懇切，不能如之何。

translations.literal: I disputed with him most earnestly but could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: I argued with all my force and could not sway him.

sentences.zh: 本出足下以為外援，而今更恨足下在外，不得相與共諫止之，或當相從耳。」

translations.literal: I had originally looked to you below as outside support, yet now all the more regret that you are outside and cannot join together in remonstrance to stop it—perhaps I ought to follow after all."
translations.idiomatic: I counted on you abroad as our ally; now I bitterly regret that you are away and cannot help me stop this—I may yet have to join you in exile."

sentences.zh: 嶠亦累書止亮。

translations.literal: Qiao also repeatedly wrote to stop Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao wrote again and again urging Liang to desist.

sentences.zh: 舉朝以為不可，亮皆不聽。

translations.literal: The whole court thought it unwise; Liang would listen to none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court opposed the plan; Liang ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 峻聞之，遣司馬何仍詣亮曰：「討賊外任，遠近惟命，至於內輔，實非所堪。」

translations.literal: Jun heard of it and sent Marshal He Reng to call on Liang, saying: "Punishing bandits in an outside appointment—near or far, I obey your command; as for assisting within, I am truly unfit."
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent his marshal He Reng to Liang with a message: "Give me an outer command against the enemy and I obey; put me at court and I am unfit."

sentences.zh: 亮不許，召北中郎將郭默為後將軍、領屯騎校尉，司徒右長史庾冰為吳國內史，皆將兵以備峻。

translations.literal: Liang did not agree; he summoned North General of the Center Guo Mo as Rear General and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, and Yu Bing, Right Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses, as Interior Minister of Wu—both leading troops to guard against Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Liang refused, posted Guo Mo as Rear General and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, and Yu Bing as interior minister of Wu, each with troops to block Jun.

sentences.zh: 冰，亮之弟也。

translations.literal: Bing was Liang's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was Yu Liang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 於是下優詔，征峻為大司農，加散騎常侍，位特進，以弟逸代領部曲。

translations.literal: Thereupon a gracious edict was issued, summoning Jun as Minister of the Imperial Granary, adding Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and the rank of Special Advance, with his younger brother Yi replacing him in command of his private troops.
translations.idiomatic: A flattering edict then summoned Jun to the post of Minister of the Imperial Granary with the rank of Special Advance, replacing him with his brother Yi over his personal troops.

sentences.zh: 峻上表曰：「昔明皇帝親執臣手，使臣北討胡寇。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly Emperor Ming personally took my hand and sent me north to punish the barbarian raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized: "Emperor Ming once took my hand in his and sent me north against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 今中原未靖，臣何敢即安！

translations.literal: Now the central plains are not yet pacified—how dare I immediately rest!
translations.idiomatic: The heartland is still unrestored—how dare I lay down my arms!

sentences.zh: 乞補青州界一荒郡，以展鷹犬之用。」

translations.literal: I beg to be assigned a wasteland commandery within Qing Province's borders, to extend the use of hawk and hound."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me some forgotten county on Qingzhou's frontier, where I may still serve as your hound."

sentences.zh: 復不許。

translations.literal: Again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again refused.

sentences.zh: 峻嚴裝將赴召，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Jun dressed in full kit and was about to go in answer to the summons, hesitating and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Jun packed for the capital but lingered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 參軍任讓謂峻曰：「將軍求處荒郡而不見許，事勢如此，恐無生路，不如勒兵自守。」

translations.literal: Adjutant Ren Rang said to Jun: "General, you sought a wasteland commandery and were not granted it; matters stand thus—I fear there is no way to live; better to array troops and hold by yourself."
translations.idiomatic: His adjutant Ren Rang said, "You asked for a backwater post and were denied; in this fix there may be no survival except to muster your men and stand your ground."

sentences.zh: 阜陵令匡術亦勸峻反，峻遂不應命。

translations.literal: Fuling Magistrate Kuang Shu also urged Jun to rebel; Jun thereupon did not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling magistrate Kuang Shu urged rebellion too, and Jun defied the summons.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠聞之，即欲帥眾下衛建康，三吳亦欲起義兵；

translations.literal: Wen Qiao heard of it and at once wished to lead his forces down to guard Jiankang; the Three Wu regions also wished to raise righteous troops;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao wanted to march his army to defend Jiankang; the Three Wu regions prepared to rise as well;

sentences.zh: 亮並不聽，而報嶠書曰：「吾憂西陲，過於歷陽，足下無過雷池一步也。」

translations.literal: Liang would listen to none of it, and replied to Qiao in a letter, saying: "My worry is the western frontier, more than Liyang—you below must not cross one step beyond Leichi."
translations.idiomatic: Liang forbade both and wrote Qiao: "The western frontier troubles me more than Liyang—do not cross Leichi by a single step."

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使諭峻，峻曰：「台下雲我欲反，豈得活邪！

translations.literal: The court sent a messenger to instruct Jun; Jun said: "The platform below says I wish to rebel—how could I be allowed to live!
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys; Jun replied, "The court already calls me a rebel—how could I survive if I obey!

sentences.zh: 我寧山頭望廷尉，不能廷尉望山頭。

translations.literal: I would rather stand on the mountaintop looking toward the Commandant of Justice than have the Commandant of Justice look toward the mountaintop.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather face trial from my hilltop than mount the scaffold under their gaze.

sentences.zh: 往者國家危如累卵，非我不濟；

translations.literal: Formerly when the state was precarious as piled eggs, but for me it would not have been saved;
translations.idiomatic: When the realm hung by a thread, none but I saved it;

sentences.zh: 狡兔既死，獵犬宜烹。

translations.literal: Once the cunning rabbit is dead, the hunting dog ought to be boiled.
translations.idiomatic: once the rabbit is caught, the hound goes into the pot.

sentences.zh: 但當死報造謀者耳！」

translations.literal: I ought only to die repaying those who plotted this!"
translations.idiomatic: I can only repay the plotters with my death—or theirs!"

sentences.zh: 峻知祖約怨朝廷，乃遣參軍徐會推崇約，請共討庾亮。

translations.literal: Jun knew Zu Yue resented the court; thereupon he sent adjutant Xu Hui to extol Yue and ask to join in attacking Yu Liang together.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zu Yue's grudge against the court, Jun sent Xu Hui to flatter him and propose a joint strike on Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 約大喜，其從子智、衍並勸成之。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly pleased; his nephew Zhi and Yan both urged him to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was delighted; his nephews Zhi and Yan both urged him to agree.

sentences.zh: 譙國內史桓宣謂智曰：「本以強胡未滅，將戮力討之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, Interior Minister of Qiao, said to Zhi: "Originally, because the strong barbarians were not yet destroyed, we were to exert our strength together to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, interior minister of Qiao, told Zhi, "We were supposed to unite against the barbarians while they still threatened us.

sentences.zh: 使君若欲為雄霸，何不助國討峻，則威名自舉。

translations.literal: If my lord wishes to become a heroic hegemon, why not help the state punish Jun—then renown would raise itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you seek greatness, help the court crush Jun and your fame will rise of itself.

sentences.zh: 今乃與峻俱反，此安得久乎！」

translations.literal: Now you join Jun in rebellion together—how can this last long!"
translations.idiomatic: Join Jun in rebellion and how long can that endure!"

sentences.zh: 智不從。

translations.literal: Zhi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi refused.

sentences.zh: 宣詣約請見，約知其欲諫，拒而不內。

translations.literal: Xuan went to Yue to request an audience; Yue knew he wished to remonstrate and refused him, not admitting him within.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sought an audience with Yue; Yue guessed his purpose and shut him out.

sentences.zh: 宣遂絕約，不與之同。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon broke with Yue and would not join with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan broke with Yue and would have no part of the plot.

sentences.zh: 十一月，約遣兄子沛內史渙、女婿淮南太守許柳以兵會峻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yue sent his elder brother's son Huan, Interior Minister of Pei, and his son-in-law Xu Liu, Administrator of Huainan, with troops to join Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yue sent his nephew Huan, interior minister of Pei, and his son-in-law Xu Liu, governor of Huainan, with troops to join Jun.

sentences.zh: 逖妻，柳之姊也，固諫，不從。

translations.literal: Zu Ti's wife was Liu's elder sister; she firmly remonstrated, but he would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti's widow, Xu Liu's elder sister, pleaded against it in vain.

sentences.zh: 詔復以卞壺為尚書令、領右衛將軍，以會稽內史王舒行揚州刺史事，吳興太守虞潭督三吳等諸郡軍事。

translations.literal: An edict again made Bian Hu Director of the Masters of Writing and Commander of the Right Guard, made Wang Shu, Interior Minister of Kuaiji, act as Inspector of Yang Province, and made Yu Tan, Administrator of Wuxing, Supervisor of military affairs for the Three Wu and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored Bian Hu as Director of the Masters of Writing and Right Guard commander, put Wang Shu of Kuaiji in charge of Yangzhou, and made Yu Tan of Wuxing overseer of the Three Wu armies.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞孔坦、司徒司馬丹楊陶回言於王導，請「及峻未至，急斷阜陵，守江西當利諸口，彼少我眾，一戰決矣。

translations.literal: Kong Tan, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, and Tao Hui, Steward of Danyang and Marshal of the Minister over the Masses, spoke to Wang Dao, requesting: "Before Jun arrives, urgently cut off Fuling and hold the mouths at Dangli and elsewhere west of the river—they are fewer, we are many; one battle will decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan, left assistant director of the Masters of Writing, and Tao Hui, steward of Danyang and marshal to the Minister over the Masses, urged Wang Dao: "Before Jun arrives, seal off Fuling and hold the Yangzi crossings at Dangli—their numbers are few and ours many; one battle will settle it.

sentences.zh: 若峻未來，可往逼其城。

translations.literal: If Jun has not yet come, we can go and press his city.
translations.idiomatic: If he has not marched yet, advance and threaten his base.

sentences.zh: 今不先往，峻必先至，峻至則人心危駭，難與戰矣。

translations.literal: If we do not go first now, Jun will certainly arrive first; when Jun arrives, people's hearts will be perilously terrified—it will be hard to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wait, and Jun reaches us first; once he does, panic will break morale and the fight will be lost.

sentences.zh: 此時不可失也。」

translations.literal: This moment cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: The moment must not be wasted."

sentences.zh: 導然之，庾亮不從。

translations.literal: Dao agreed; Yu Liang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Dao agreed; Yu Liang again refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，蘇峻使其將韓晃、張健等襲陷姑孰，取鹽米，亮方悔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Xinhai, Su Jun sent his generals Han Huang, Zhang Jian, and others to raid and seize Gudu, taking its salt and grain; only then did Liang regret his course.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day Xinhai, Su Jun sent his generals Han Huang and Zhang Jian to storm Gudu and seize its salt and grain; Yu Liang finally regretted what he had done.

sentences.zh: 壬子，彭城王雄、章武王休叛奔峻。
